rst-1-q334.objective: Isolate chipped items or fragments when found and handle chemicals correctly.
rst-1-q334.stem: Why display dilution instructions for detergents and disinfectants?
options: To encourage estimating by eye
So everyone can prepare the correct concentration
To remove the need to read labels
To hide chemical names
rst-1-q334.explanation: Clear instructions based on product requirements prevent concentration errors.

rst-1-q335.objective: Classify food safety hazards and stop use and report when an abnormality is found.
rst-1-q335.stem: Why is heating alone insufficient when metal fragments may be in food?
options: Metal always becomes bacteria
Heating makes food weigh zero
Ordinary heating cannot remove hard foreign objects
Refrigeration always melts them
rst-1-q335.explanation: Physical foreign objects differ from microbial hazards and require contamination prevention and isolation of affected items.

rst-1-q336.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q336.stem: Which Japanese banknote denomination is listed in the textbook?
rst-1-q336.explanation: The 2,000-yen note is a Japanese banknote. Follow the restaurant’s checking procedure if unfamiliar with it.

rst-1-q337.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-q337.stem: How should you hold a plug when unplugging it?
options: Hold the plug body, not the cord
Pull hard on the middle of the cord
Grip metal parts with wet hands
Pour water on the socket while unplugging
rst-1-q337.explanation: Hold the plug to avoid damaging the cord and do not touch it with wet hands.

rst-1-q338.objective: Apply the three principles for preventing bacterial food poisoning throughout the work process.
rst-1-q338.stem: Why are heating and other controls still needed after thawing frozen food?
options: Freezing does not kill every bacterium
Freezing always removes all bacteria
Thawing makes shelf life unlimited
Packaging removes the need for handwashing
rst-1-q338.explanation: Freezing suppresses growth but is not disinfection. Continue food-appropriate controls after thawing.

rst-1-q339.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q339.stem: Which set of Japanese coin denominations is correct?
rst-1-q339.explanation: The textbook lists coins of 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, and 500 yen.

rst-1-q340.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-q340.stem: Why pay attention to dust between sockets and plugs?
options: To check food seasonality
To increase steam
To store refrigerated food at room temperature
To help prevent electrical fires
rst-1-q340.explanation: Dust around electrical equipment and cord damage are also part of daily fire-prevention checks.

rst-1-q341.objective: Classify food safety hazards and stop use and report when an abnormality is found.
rst-1-q341.stem: Which food-poisoning cause category do Anisakis and roundworms share?
options: Viruses
Chemicals
Parasites
Bacteria
rst-1-q341.explanation: The textbook gives Anisakis and roundworms as examples of parasitic causes of food poisoning.

rst-1-q342.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q342.stem: Which debit-card payment feature is appropriate?
options: The amount is deducted from the account immediately
Charges are always combined the following year
All are exclusively prepaid
They only work with paper meal tickets
rst-1-q342.explanation: The textbook describes debit cards as deducting the amount from the account when used.

rst-1-q343.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-q343.stem: Where should flammable spray cans not be stored?
options: A designated place meeting product conditions
A hot place in direct sun or near flames
A safe place separate from food
A temperature-checked storage location
rst-1-q343.explanation: Store flammable spray cans appropriately away from high temperatures and flames.

rst-1-q344.objective: Explain why hazards other than bacteria cannot be assessed by ordinary heating or refrigeration alone.
rst-1-q344.stem: Why does visual parasite inspection alone not complete all controls?
options: Food-appropriate treatment and control conditions must also be checked
Visually inspected fish are all sterile
Raw internal organs may then be served
Refrigeration becomes unnecessary
rst-1-q344.explanation: Combine visual checks, gut removal, and necessary freezing or heating with measures suited to the food.

rst-1-q345.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q345.stem: Which credit-card feature matches the textbook?
options: Always depositing all cash first
Always deducting the entire balance immediately
Reading banknotes
Deferred payment
rst-1-q345.explanation: The textbook classifies credit cards as deferred payment. Check which brands the restaurant accepts.

rst-1-q346.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-q346.stem: Why keep waste frying-oil containers away from fire sources?
options: To always return oil to edible use
To reduce fire risk
To remove oil weight
To fill them with water
rst-1-q346.explanation: Manage waste oil in covered containers and do not place them near flames.

rst-1-q347.objective: Identify fish parts as instructed and explain seasonality including regional differences.
rst-1-q347.stem: What is the part covering a fish’s gills called?
options: Lateral line
Gill cover
Dorsal fin
Tail fin
rst-1-q347.explanation: The fish diagram identifies the gill cover as covering the gills, distinct from fins and the lateral line.

rst-1-q348.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q348.stem: Which payment method is introduced as a top-up type?
options: All credit cards
All debit cards
Electronic money
Cash change
rst-1-q348.explanation: The textbook gives electronic money as a top-up example. Check the actual method against the restaurant’s contract and product.

rst-1-q349.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-q349.stem: Which basic extinguisher operation order is correct?
options: Squeeze lever → reinsert pin → turn away
Pull pin → aim nozzle at fire source → squeeze lever
Aim at a person → pull pin → throw it
Open the body → remove contents by hand
rst-1-q349.explanation: The textbook’s order is pin, nozzle, lever. Prioritize evacuation over unsafe firefighting.

rst-1-q350.objective: Check refrigerator temperature, storage limits, and abnormality responses as a connected process.
rst-1-q350.stem: What should be checked when choosing refrigerator items to use first during expiry checks?
options: Only container size
Only staff preferences
Only whether an item is at the front
Each food’s label and usable time limit
rst-1-q350.explanation: Check expiry limits along with cold storage and use food within its limit.

rst-1-q351.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q351.stem: When a customer scans the restaurant’s code to pay, what is necessary?
options: Treat everything as complete without checking the screen
Always charge again after scanning
Check the amount and payment result by restaurant procedure
Take duplicate cash first
rst-1-q351.explanation: Check the amount and payment result using the restaurant’s method, not just that the code was scanned.

rst-1-q352.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q352.stem: Which feature of beef inside round matches the textbook?
options: It is entirely bone
Low fat
The highest fat content
Always classified as offal
rst-1-q352.explanation: The textbook identifies inside round as a low-fat beef cut.

rst-1-q353.objective: Break contamination routes from raw ingredients to prepared food.
rst-1-q353.stem: Raw-meat packaging has meat juice outside. Which route beyond the food needs attention?
options: Only knife length
Contamination through hands and handles
Only plating colors
Only food-name pronunciation
rst-1-q353.explanation: Dirt outside containers can transfer through hands and equipment to other food.

rst-1-q354.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-q354.stem: Why check which cashless methods the restaurant accepts?
options: The same terminal accepts all methods regardless of contract
Accepting cards means accepting all electronic money
A customer app removes the need to check restaurant support
Support differs by contract and terminal
rst-1-q354.explanation: Know the latest accepted methods because availability depends on the restaurant’s contract and equipment.

rst-1-q355.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q355.stem: Which way of preparing beef outside round for stir-frying matches the textbook?
options: Warm a large block only briefly
Add connective tissue and serve raw
Slice thinly or cut into small pieces
Add only fat and freeze
rst-1-q355.explanation: Outside round is a somewhat firm lean cut; examples include thin slicing or small pieces for stir-frying.

rst-1-q356.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q356.stem: Which colander materials are introduced in the textbook?
options: Only paper and cloth
Only ceramics and glass
Only cardboard and foam paper
Stainless steel and plastic
rst-1-q356.explanation: Examples include stainless-steel and plastic colanders. Use one suited to purpose and temperature.

rst-1-q357.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q357.stem: What should you say when a complaint exceeds your authority?
options: Explain that you will call the responsible person and report promptly
Always promise a refund yourself
Leave for a long time without explanation
Move the guest without listening
rst-1-q357.explanation: When a decision is difficult, explain to the customer and refer to the responsible person.

rst-1-q358.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q358.stem: What description do beef katabara and tomobara share?
options: Lean and fat form layers
They consist only of offal
They contain no fat
All are always as tender as tenderloin
rst-1-q358.explanation: Both have layered lean and fat. Also check firmness and suitability for dishes.

rst-1-q359.objective: Separate cleaning tools and worn equipment and clean contact surfaces too.
rst-1-q359.stem: What is wrong with touching a kitchen handle with gloves used for toilet cleaning?
options: Dry glove surfaces cannot transfer contamination
No change is needed without direct food contact
Later wiping the handle means gloves need not be changed immediately
Contamination may spread elsewhere
rst-1-q359.explanation: Pay attention to equipment-removal order and touched surfaces to avoid carrying contamination out of the cleaning area.

rst-1-q360.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q360.stem: Why mainly preserve a dish containing a foreign object?
options: To give it to another guest
To remove the object and serve it again
To examine the item and investigate cause and impact
To skip all records
rst-1-q360.explanation: Preserve the dish and object by restaurant procedure for checks by the responsible person and kitchen.

rst-1-q361.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q361.stem: Whose input is needed when deciding to remake a dish containing a foreign object?
options: Only neighboring guests
Only the delivery company
The customer’s wishes and the restaurant’s responsible person
Only your own wishes
rst-1-q361.explanation: Handle remakes and charges after checking customer wishes and restaurant authority and rules.

rst-1-q362.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q362.stem: What is bone-in pork belly called?
options: Sirloin
Chicken tender
Spare ribs
Rump
rst-1-q362.explanation: The textbook calls bone-in pork belly spare ribs. Distinguish the animal and cut.

rst-1-q363.objective: Express welcome and apologies with clean appearance and calm movements.
rst-1-q363.stem: Which fragrance consideration is appropriate for service appearance?
options: Avoid strong perfume
Cover sweat only with strong perfume
Change strong perfume for each dish
Strong fragrance makes uniform dirt irrelevant
rst-1-q363.explanation: The textbook says to avoid strong perfume. Maintain cleanliness and restrained grooming suited to dining.

rst-1-q364.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q364.stem: How should a complaint identifying a bone as a foreign object be received?
options: Always exclude bones from complaints
Give it to another guest without inspection
Check it as a hazard and complaint even if it is part of an ingredient
Declare the customer wrong
rst-1-q364.explanation: Ingredient parts such as bones can still cause injuries and complaints. Check the circumstances and item.

rst-1-q365.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-q365.stem: Which beef rump description matches the textbook?
options: Only bone and skin
Tender lean meat with depth of flavor
The most connective tissue of every cut
Chopped offal
rst-1-q365.explanation: Beef rump is described as tender lean meat used in many dishes, including steak.

rst-1-q366.objective: Wash hands when changing tasks and clean thoroughly, including fingertips and thumbs.
rst-1-q366.stem: What does the textbook state about washing hands twice?
options: Only wear two gloves
Repeat washing with soap and rinsing
Wipe hands on ingredients afterward
Only increase alcohol applications
rst-1-q366.explanation: It describes repeating the steps from soap washing through running-water rinsing as effective.

rst-1-q367.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q367.stem: What is appropriate when unsure whether to charge for food in a foreign-object complaint?
options: The staff member decides everyone’s bill
Discard the item and continue payment
Interrupt the customer to demand payment
Consult the restaurant’s responsible person
rst-1-q367.explanation: Charges and compensation follow authority and rules. Consult the responsible person.

rst-1-q368.objective: Identify fish parts as instructed and explain seasonality including regional differences.
rst-1-q368.stem: Which seafood is given as an autumn example?
options: Wakame
Bonito
Snow crab
Crucian carp
rst-1-q368.explanation: Autumn examples include bonito. Check actual seasonality and deliveries, including production areas.

rst-1-q369.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q369.stem: Which utensil is listed together with “kettle”?
options: Stockpot
Yukihira saucepan
Wok
Water kettle
rst-1-q369.explanation: The utensil list gives yakan and kettle together. Match restaurant terminology to the actual item.

rst-1-q370.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q370.stem: Why mainly avoid paper clips and staplers near food?
options: To raise food temperature
To dry dishes faster
To increase change
To prevent metal and other foreign-object contamination
rst-1-q370.explanation: Do not use them near food to prevent small metal pieces and similar objects entering it.

rst-1-q371.objective: Use major vegetable categories and approximate seasons in ingredient checks and customer guidance.
rst-1-q371.stem: Which category includes eggplant, tomato, and cucumber?
options: Root vegetables
Fruit vegetables
Leaf and stem vegetables
Vegetables eaten as sweet fruit
rst-1-q371.explanation: The textbook classifies them as fruit vegetables because the fruit is used.

rst-1-q372.objective: Classify dishes by process and control temperature and time until service for unheated dishes.
rst-1-q372.stem: Which range is closely related to avoiding prolonged holding in the danger zone?
options: Only −30 to −20℃
Only below 0℃
Only above 100℃
rst-1-q372.explanation: The textbook describes 10–60℃ as a zone favorable to bacterial growth, controlled together with time.

rst-1-q373.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-q373.stem: After catching an insect in the seating area, what should still be checked?
options: Record only the number caught and stop investigating
Causes of breeding or entry
Check only seating, not routes to the kitchen
Assume more chemicals remove the need to check entry routes
rst-1-q373.explanation: To prevent contamination, investigate and improve causes of insect breeding or entry, not just remove insects.

rst-1-q374.objective: Use major vegetable categories and approximate seasons in ingredient checks and customer guidance.
rst-1-q374.stem: Which season is given for bamboo shoots, rapeseed blossoms, and asparagus?
options: Summer
Autumn
Spring
Winter
rst-1-q374.explanation: The textbook lists them as spring examples. Origin and climate can cause variation.

rst-1-q375.objective: Connect cooking methods with checks at the center of food and stop serving if heating is insufficient.
rst-1-q375.stem: Why does oil at 180℃ not mean the food’s center is also 180℃?
options: Oil and food interiors are different measurement locations
Food has no center
Oil temperature shows weight
All thermometers display the same value
rst-1-q375.explanation: Heating-medium and core temperatures differ. Check at the required position.

rst-1-q376.objective: Ensure safety, communicate symptoms, request emergency help when necessary, and coordinate within the restaurant.
rst-1-q376.stem: A guest has altered consciousness and swallowing ability is uncertain. What should be avoided?
options: Calling for help
Arranging an emergency call
Following dispatcher instructions
Forcing water on them
rst-1-q376.explanation: Do not force food or drink when consciousness or swallowing is impaired. Follow emergency instructions.

rst-1-q377.objective: Prepare the required quantity and prevent temperature rises and contamination during preparation.
rst-1-q377.stem: Which preparation example adds seasoning in advance?
options: Discarding after completion
Erasing ingredient names
Marinating in seasonings
Disinfecting dishes
rst-1-q377.explanation: Preparation includes quantity calculations, washing, cutting, and preseasoning such as marinating.

rst-1-q378.objective: Understand the risks of leaving food after cooking and link cooling, storage, and reheating records.
rst-1-q378.stem: What facts should be recorded when cooling equipment is used?
options: Actual cooling times and temperatures
Only equipment name, omitting temperature
Only the planned final reading
A mark deciding in advance there is no abnormality
rst-1-q378.explanation: Equipment use alone does not prove conditions were met. Check actual time and temperature according to the plan.

rst-1-q379.objective: Ensure safety, communicate symptoms, request emergency help when necessary, and coordinate within the restaurant.
rst-1-q379.stem: What information should be ready to give first when calling emergency services?
options: Today’s sales and spending per guest
Restaurant location and the guest’s condition
Every employee’s work history
Only plating photos
rst-1-q379.explanation: Give location, symptoms, consciousness, and breathing details so responders can arrive and understand the situation.

rst-1-q380.objective: Connect cutting names with finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
rst-1-q380.stem: What shape feature results from cutting ingredients diagonally?
options: Always becoming spherical
A larger cut surface
Identical cubes
Always quartering a round
rst-1-q380.explanation: Diagonal cutting of long ingredients increases the cut surface area.

rst-1-q381.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-q381.stem: Why separate important-control records by dish process?
options: To heat all food identically
To hide dish names
To eliminate checks after service
Checkpoints differ by dish
rst-1-q381.explanation: Unheated, heated, cooled, and reheated processes have different controls. Use process-appropriate records.

rst-1-q382.objective: Ensure safety, communicate symptoms, request emergency help when necessary, and coordinate within the restaurant.
rst-1-q382.stem: What comes before investigating the cause of a suspected severe allergic reaction?
options: Costing every product
Calling for assistance and necessary emergency help
Completing all cleaning
Taking advance payment
rst-1-q382.explanation: In urgent situations, prioritize safety and emergency response and pass known information to medical personnel.

rst-1-q383.objective: Connect cutting names with finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
options: A half-round cut in half again
Thick rounds
Extremely fine julienne
Uniform cubes
rst-1-q383.explanation: The textbook describes shiraga as extremely fine julienne, distinct from other shapes and sizes.

rst-1-q384.objective: Classify food safety hazards and stop use and report when an abnormality is found.
rst-1-q384.stem: What is appropriate for food whose bacteria or foreign objects are not visible?
options: Apply necessary hygiene controls even if it looks normal
No odor always means harmless
Anything transparent is drinkable
Tasting alone reveals every hazard
rst-1-q384.explanation: Microorganisms and chemicals may not be visible. Controls suited to the process are necessary.

rst-1-q385.objective: Ensure safety, communicate symptoms, request emergency help when necessary, and coordinate within the restaurant.
rst-1-q385.stem: Which role allocation is appropriate while waiting for emergency responders?
options: Everyone returns to the kitchen
Leave the guest alone while everyone records
Everyone handles only payment
Assign monitoring, calling, and guiding responders separately
rst-1-q385.explanation: Coordinate monitoring the guest, calling, and ensuring access for responders.

rst-1-q386.objective: Match equipment names to their functions and distinguish heating, hot holding, cooling, and storage.
rst-1-q386.stem: What is the main use introduced for a tilting kettle?
options: Making only one person’s ice
Large-batch stir-frying and simmering
Only measuring food surface temperature
Filling glasses with water
rst-1-q386.explanation: A tilting kettle is introduced for stir-frying and simmering in large-volume cooking.

rst-1-q387.objective: Apply the three principles for preventing bacterial food poisoning throughout the work process.
rst-1-q387.stem: Which principle covers handling cooked food with clean utensils?
options: Do not contaminate
Only prevent growth
Only freeze
Reduce weight
rst-1-q387.explanation: Clean hands and utensils prevent bacteria from contaminating food.

rst-1-q388.objective: Ensure personal safety before acting according to restaurant roles and evacuation plans.
rst-1-q388.stem: What is the first priority during continuing violent shaking?
options: Run into a dangerous kitchen
Put away every dish
Calculate sales
Protect yourself from falling objects
rst-1-q388.explanation: Ensure your own safety first and, where possible, call on customers to protect themselves.

rst-1-q389.objective: Match equipment names to their functions and distinguish heating, hot holding, cooling, and storage.
rst-1-q389.stem: Which equipment combines display and refrigerated storage?
options: Fryer
Jet oven
Noodle boiler
Refrigerated display case
rst-1-q389.explanation: A refrigerated display case displays food while keeping it refrigerated.

rst-1-q390.objective: Understand sources of major bacteria and select prevention suited to the food and task.
rst-1-q390.stem: Why avoid leaving cooked dishes out when spore-forming bacteria are a concern?
options: Heating records remove the need for cooling
Room-temperature holding always kills bacteria
Growth during cooling and storage must also be prevented
A large pot guarantees safety
rst-1-q390.explanation: Continue temperature and time control after heating and avoid prolonged conditions favorable to growth.

rst-1-q391.objective: Ensure personal safety before acting according to restaurant roles and evacuation plans.
rst-1-q391.stem: What should a restaurant in a tsunami-risk area check in advance?
options: Only plating order
Only next month’s bookings
Evacuation destinations such as high ground and routes
Only food-label colors
rst-1-q391.explanation: Check destinations and methods suited to local risks in the restaurant plan to enable guidance during an event.

rst-1-q392.objective: Relate dishwashing and ingredient-processing equipment to its purpose and safe operation.
rst-1-q392.stem: What is the main purpose of a peeler?
options: Boiling noodles
Removing ingredient skins
Measuring food core temperature
Keeping rice warm
rst-1-q392.explanation: Match equipment names to purposes and use the method in which you have been trained.

rst-1-q393.objective: Explain why hazards other than bacteria cannot be assessed by ordinary heating or refrigeration alone.
rst-1-q393.stem: Which explanation of norovirus is incorrect?
options: It can spread from feces
It can spread from vomit
It can never spread from anything other than bivalve shellfish
Handwashing is important
rst-1-q393.explanation: Contamination through infected people also occurs, so controlling bivalve shellfish alone is not enough.

rst-1-q394.objective: Ensure personal safety before acting according to restaurant roles and evacuation plans.
rst-1-q394.stem: After beginning fire evacuation, you remember a forgotten item. What should you do?
options: Return if alone
Always return if no smoke is visible
Ask another guest to retrieve it
Do not return; tell the responsible person from a safe place
rst-1-q394.explanation: Do not return toward the fire after evacuating, and watch that customers do not return either.

rst-1-q395.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-q395.stem: Which purpose pairing appropriately distinguishes a whisk and a colander?
options: Mixing and draining
Core-temperature measurement and freezing
Ice making and vacuum packing
Floor cleaning and toilet disinfection
rst-1-q395.explanation: Use utensils for their purposes and keep food-contact parts clean.

rst-1-q396.objective: Check both order details and hygiene condition to identify unacceptable items.
rst-1-q396.stem: How should use-by and best-before labels be understood at receiving?
options: Do not treat them as identical; check labels and storage conditions
Both become unlimited under refrigeration
Ignore damaged packaging for best-before items
Do not compare dates if the words look similar
rst-1-q396.explanation: The two labels have different meanings. Match label type, date, and storage conditions before accepting.

rst-1-q397.objective: Ensure personal safety before acting according to restaurant roles and evacuation plans.
rst-1-q397.stem: What should the person guiding evacuation during a fire do?
options: Gather everyone at the fire source
Stack equipment in guest passageways
Clearly announce the safe evacuation route in a loud voice
Leave alone without notifying anyone
rst-1-q397.explanation: Follow assigned roles and clearly guide people along safe routes avoiding smoke and fire.

rst-1-q398.objective: Measure weight, core temperature, surface temperature, and time using appropriate instruments.
rst-1-q398.stem: A faulty scale gives unstable readings. How should recipe quantities be checked?
options: Tell the responsible person and use verified alternative equipment
Choose only a convenient reading
Treat container-inclusive weight as net weight
Estimate all ingredients by eye
rst-1-q398.explanation: Do not decide using uncertain measurements. Report the fault and confirm a reliable measuring method.

rst-1-q399.objective: Check refrigerator temperature, storage limits, and abnormality responses as a connected process.
rst-1-q399.stem: A food label requires a stricter temperature than a general refrigerator example. What approach applies?
options: Check that food’s label and the restaurant standard
Use the general example for every food
Ignore expiry dates if cold
Change to a warmer temperature if easier
rst-1-q399.explanation: Do not apply textbook temperature examples universally. Follow each food’s storage conditions and the restaurant management plan.

rst-1-q400.objective: Ensure personal safety before acting according to restaurant roles and evacuation plans.
rst-1-q400.stem: Broken glass is at an exit after an earthquake. What is needed before guiding guests?
options: Rush everyone through the same exit
Tell them to run without avoiding glass
Return to seating only to pay
Check another route that can be used safely
rst-1-q400.explanation: Check surroundings even after shaking stops and guide guests along a safe route.

rst-1-week02-q01.objective: Check refrigerator temperature, storage limits, and abnormality responses as a connected process.
rst-1-week02-q01.stem: The restaurant refrigerator standard is 10℃ or below, but the opening reading is 12℃. What should be recorded?
options: Only the 10℃ standard
A mark deciding in advance there is no abnormality
The actual 12℃ reading and reports/actions
Only the setting
rst-1-week02-q01.explanation: Record actual measurements and abnormality responses and check food handling with the responsible person.

rst-1-week02-q02.objective: Check refrigerator temperature, storage limits, and abnormality responses as a connected process.
rst-1-week02-q02.stem: A refrigerator containing in-date food had a prolonged temperature fault. Which view is correct?
options: In-date food needs no temperature check
Closing the door makes everything immediately servable
Just erase temperature records
Check temperature history even for in-date food
rst-1-week02-q02.explanation: Both expiry limits and temperature matter; being in date alone cannot establish safety.

rst-1-week02-q03.objective: Break contamination routes from raw ingredients to prepared food.
rst-1-week02-q03.stem: A raw-fish container leaks onto packaging of cooked food below. What decision is most needed?
options: Separate affected items and request a check
Replace only the fish container and use everything
Assume wiping visible juice guarantees safety
Rename the food and serve it first
rst-1-week02-q03.explanation: Contamination can spread to food, packaging, and hands. Check the affected scope and obtain instructions.

rst-1-week02-q04.objective: Break contamination routes from raw ingredients to prepared food.
rst-1-week02-q04.stem: Meat and vegetable knives were in the same unwashed tray. What preparation comes next?
options: Label only the vegetable knife and use it
Remove only the meat knife and use the rest unchecked
Just wipe off moisture and resume separation
Check both for cleanliness and treat as needed
rst-1-week02-q04.explanation: Check actual contact and cleanliness, not just labels. Wash and disinfect appropriately before use.

rst-1-week02-q05.objective: Remove dirt before proper disinfection and prevent chemical mix-ups.
rst-1-week02-q05.stem: You must chemically treat washed utensils. What should guide procedure selection?
options: Only a senior worker’s visual estimate
Only container appearance
Conditions suited to the material and chemical label
Any strongest solution
rst-1-week02-q05.explanation: Check suitable methods and concentrations against product labels and restaurant procedures.

rst-1-week02-q06.objective: Remove dirt before proper disinfection and prevent chemical mix-ups.
rst-1-week02-q06.stem: A decanted chemical’s label is fading. What is appropriate?
options: Verify contents and ensure clear labeling and storage
Use it if the smell is similar
Transfer it to an unlabeled food bottle
Identify it only by text color
rst-1-week02-q06.explanation: Do not use unidentified contents. Ensure clear labels and dedicated containers to prevent mix-ups.

rst-1-week02-q07.objective: Separate cleaning tools and worn equipment and clean contact surfaces too.
rst-1-week02-q07.stem: Gloves become dirty during toilet cleaning. What should happen before leaving the area?
options: Use them to open the kitchen handle
Follow equipment and hand-hygiene procedures before moving
Wipe them on an apron and plate food
Double gloves and handle food
rst-1-week02-q07.explanation: Follow transition procedures including equipment handling and handwashing to avoid spreading contamination.

rst-1-week02-q08.objective: Check personal health and appearance and report food-related abnormalities without hiding them.
rst-1-week02-q08.stem: At opening checks, one worker has diarrhea and another a hand wound. What approach is correct?
options: Give everyone identical gloves
Each reports and checks work eligibility and protection
Continue food work if they say they are fine
Change work without recording symptoms
rst-1-week02-q08.explanation: Illness and wounds need different responses. Tell the responsible person to prevent effects on food.

rst-1-week03-q01.objective: Wash hands when changing tasks and clean thoroughly, including fingertips and thumbs.
rst-1-week03-q01.stem: Handwashing was performed but fingertips were missed. What should the checker advise?
options: Repeat the procedure including fingertips
Finish if palms are clean
Rub only fingertips with a dry cloth
Double gloves and skip washing
rst-1-week03-q01.explanation: Identify missed areas specifically and follow washing, rinsing, and drying steps.

rst-1-week03-q02.objective: Wash hands when changing tasks and clean thoroughly, including fingertips and thumbs.
rst-1-week03-q02.stem: After soap and running-water washing, you plan to continue with wet hands. What step is needed?
options: Touch food to remove moisture
Wipe on work clothes
Dry using a clean method
Use a dirty shared towel
rst-1-week03-q02.explanation: Drying is part of handwashing. Avoid recontamination from dirty items.

rst-1-week03-q03.objective: Tidy and clean according to a plan and manage waste separately from food.
rst-1-week03-q03.stem: A weekly cleaning area is repeatedly forgotten. What helps connect it to routine work?
options: Delete it from the list
Wait for someone to remember without assigning it
Mark complete while still dirty
Specify location, date, person, and verification
rst-1-week03-q03.explanation: Set a specific plan and implementation checks to sustain cleaning.

rst-1-week03-q04.objective: Tidy and clean according to a plan and manage waste separately from food.
rst-1-week03-q04.stem: Food waste fills a container during cooking. What protects food?
options: Empty it beside finished dishes
Remove it without affecting work and restore the container
Remove the lid and pile more
Keep transferring it to clean food bowls
rst-1-week03-q04.explanation: Separate waste appropriately and prevent contamination of food and work surroundings.

rst-1-week03-q05.objective: Classify dishes by process and control temperature and time until service for unheated dishes.
rst-1-week03-q05.stem: Sashimi service will be delayed. What is especially important in an unheated process?
options: Leave it at room temperature planning to grill later
Rename it to omit temperature checks
Leave it if no dirt is visible
Keep it cold and clean until service
rst-1-week03-q05.explanation: Unheated dishes lack a final cooking step, so prevent contamination and control temperature and time.

rst-1-week03-q06.objective: Classify dishes by process and control temperature and time until service for unheated dishes.
rst-1-week03-q06.stem: How does salad made with boiled and cooled ingredients differ from raw-vegetable salad?
options: The former also needs post-cooking cooling controls
The same name means identical processes
Only the latter needs clean dishes
The former needs no refrigeration
rst-1-week03-q06.explanation: Classify by actual process rather than name and control heating and cooling where present.

rst-1-week03-q07.objective: Connect cooking methods with checks at the center of food and stop serving if heating is insufficient.
rst-1-week03-q07.stem: Meat thickness changes greatly with the same recipe. What should be checked before serving?
options: Use the old time and assume completion
Check core heating at the new thickness
Record only outer browning
Record the equipment setting as core temperature
rst-1-week03-q07.explanation: Size changes heat transfer. Verify sufficient heating under the actual conditions.

rst-1-week03-q08.objective: Understand the risks of leaving food after cooking and link cooling, storage, and reheating records.
rst-1-week03-q08.stem: Cooling start time is known but intermediate temperatures were not measured. What is appropriate?
options: Fill in planned readings afterward
Assume refrigeration means no problem
Report actual history and check against the plan
Finish based only on appearance
rst-1-week03-q08.explanation: Do not mark unchecked steps as done. Consult the responsible person using actual time and temperature facts.

rst-1-week04-q01.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-week04-q01.stem: A hygiene plan specifies checks and implementation records contain results. Which use is correct?
options: Check according to the plan and record actual results
Skip daily checks because a plan exists
Create records without reading the plan
Copy planned values as measurements
rst-1-week04-q01.explanation: The plan sets methods and responses; records document that day’s checks and actions.

rst-1-week04-q02.objective: Record what was checked, when and how, and actions taken when an abnormality was found.
rst-1-week04-q02.stem: A refrigerator repair record only says “handled.” What must be added?
options: Only the next check schedule
Specific facts such as initial reading, time, and action
Only repairer name
Only the normal later temperature, omitting abnormal readings
rst-1-week04-q02.explanation: Record specifically what was checked and done so events can be traced later.

rst-1-week04-q03.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-week04-q03.stem: A different tender beef cut arrives for a shin-stew instruction. What is appropriate?
options: Substitute anything if it is beef
Erase the delivery name and use it
Check the cut and effect on the dish and consult
Check only after payment
rst-1-week04-q03.explanation: Different cuts affect quality and procedures. Compare the order and actual product.

rst-1-week04-q04.objective: Relate meat fat and connective tissue characteristics to cutting and cooking method choices.
rst-1-week04-q04.stem: What information prevents confusion when ordering pork and chicken “leg”?
options: Cut name alone
Both animal species and cut
Only quantity without name
Only delivery date
rst-1-week04-q04.explanation: The same cut name means different food for different animals. Check both.

rst-1-week04-q05.objective: Identify fish parts as instructed and explain seasonality including regional differences.
rst-1-week04-q05.stem: How should you verify understanding of “near the gill cover” in fish preparation?
options: Point to the part on a diagram or actual fish
Answer only the season
Cut a similarly named fin yourself
Skip checks across species
rst-1-week04-q05.explanation: Connect names with actual parts and verify unclear instructions instead of guessing.

rst-1-week04-q06.objective: Identify fish parts as instructed and explain seasonality including regional differences.
rst-1-week04-q06.stem: Which explanation of fish seasonality on a seasonal menu is appropriate?
options: Guarantee raw safety if in season
Declare textbook seasons universal
Distinguish seasonal guidance from origin and delivery information
Use the same explanation without knowing the species
rst-1-week04-q06.explanation: Seasonality varies by region and climate. Match general guidance with actual delivery information.

rst-1-week04-q07.objective: Use major vegetable categories and approximate seasons in ingredient checks and customer guidance.
rst-1-week04-q07.stem: You do not know a new vegetable’s name. How should classification help?
options: Substitute a similarly colored name
Treat same-season vegetables as identical
Cook all fruit vegetables identically
Verify name and used part against the actual item
rst-1-week04-q07.explanation: Classification is a clue, not a replacement for checking actual names and uses.

rst-1-week04-q08.objective: Prepare the required quantity and prevent temperature rises and contamination during preparation.
rst-1-week04-q08.stem: While preparing raw ingredients you are asked to plate finished food. What preparation is needed?
options: Continue both on the same counter
Just wipe meat juice
Keep preparation gloves
Clean and separate areas, utensils, and hands
rst-1-week04-q08.explanation: Separate areas or times and prepare hands and utensils to avoid transferring contamination to finished food.

rst-1-week05-q01.objective: Connect cutting names with finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
rst-1-week05-q01.stem: For rangiri cuts in a simmered dish, what size approach is appropriate?
options: Aim for even cooking sizes despite varied shapes
Make all sizes different
Make extreme smallest/largest differences
Check only cut surfaces, never amounts
rst-1-week05-q01.explanation: Even irregular cuts cause cooking and quality variation if sizes differ excessively.

rst-1-week05-q02.objective: Connect cutting names with finished shapes and explain why uniform sizes matter.
rst-1-week05-q02.stem: What distinguishes tanzaku and hyoshigi cutting samples?
options: Only ingredient color
No distinction because shapes match
Only salt quantity
Flat pieces versus sticks
rst-1-week05-q02.explanation: Tanzaku is flat and plate-like; hyoshigi is stick-like. Check shape differences.

rst-1-week05-q03.objective: Choose browning prevention suited to ingredients and distinguish it from hygiene treatment.
rst-1-week05-q03.stem: After browning prevention, what is correct about hygiene?
options: No discoloration allows indefinite room storage
All soaking water is disinfectant
Continue required temperature and time controls
Food labels may be removed
rst-1-week05-q03.explanation: Browning prevention controls color and does not eliminate hygiene or storage requirements.

rst-1-week05-q04.objective: Identify fish processing states and confirm necessary preparation before cooking.
rst-1-week05-q04.stem: Fish ordered as fillet still contains bones. What should be checked?
options: Supplier definition and preparation required by the restaurant
Ignore bones because it is labeled
Serve unchanged despite bones
Rename the dish to avoid checks
rst-1-week05-q04.explanation: Compare processing definitions with actual items and perform the checks and preparation the dish requires.

rst-1-week05-q05.objective: Identify fish processing states and confirm necessary preparation before cooking.
rst-1-week05-q05.stem: What parts result from three-piece fish filleting?
options: Head, tail, and whole body
Only skin, scales, and gills
Only organs, eyes, and pectoral fins
Right fillet, left fillet, and backbone
rst-1-week05-q05.explanation: Three-piece filleting separates both fillets and the backbone. Head and gut preparation comes beforehand.

rst-1-week05-q06.objective: Check rice and water quantities and suitable boiling methods for consistent quality.
rst-1-week05-q06.stem: Rice quantity increases. What is appropriate before cooking?
options: Keep the original water amount
Always use the same time even if equipment is full
Check water ratio and equipment capacity
Estimate by sight without measuring
rst-1-week05-q06.explanation: Check rice/water balance and equipment capability for consistent quality.

rst-1-week05-q07.objective: Check oil and batch size to prevent uneven cooking and burns.
rst-1-week05-q07.stem: An order exceeds one frying batch. What method applies?
options: Add everything at once
Cook specified batches and share timing with service staff
Skip heating checks to serve faster
Keep using oil without checking it
rst-1-week05-q07.explanation: Respect batch limits for consistent cooking and quality and tell service staff about waiting times.

rst-1-week05-q08.objective: Check oil and batch size to prevent uneven cooking and burns.
rst-1-week05-q08.stem: A stir-fry is browned outside but heated unevenly inside. What conditions should be checked?
options: Only plating order
Heat level, batch size, and ingredient size
Only final plate temperature
Only seasoning order, ignoring batch size
rst-1-week05-q08.explanation: Heat, batch quantity, and ingredient conditions affect stir-fry finish and heating.

rst-1-week06-q01.objective: Explain cooking methods suited to dishes and check appropriately for ingredients and equipment.
rst-1-week06-q01.stem: Grilled fish and steamed dishes use the same timer. Which view is correct?
options: Check required heating for each dish and appliance
The same timer means identical conditions
Judge both finished by outer color alone
Steamed food needs no core check
rst-1-week06-q01.explanation: Heat transfer and ingredients differ. Follow dish-appropriate procedures and checks.

rst-1-week06-q02.objective: Explain cooking methods suited to dishes and check appropriately for ingredients and equipment.
rst-1-week06-q02.stem: Someone brings their face close while opening a steamer. What matters?
options: Steam is not hot, so continue
Open so steam does not hit face or hands
Open forcefully toward the body
Step back onto a wet floor
rst-1-week06-q02.explanation: Avoid hot-steam burns through safe posture and procedure.

rst-1-week06-q03.objective: Control hand and utensil hygiene and storage in processes without a final heating step.
rst-1-week06-q03.stem: You touch a dirty object during shaping. What is needed before resuming?
options: Continue if the shape holds
Wipe dirt on food
Restore clean hands and necessary gloves
Disinfect only after finishing
rst-1-week06-q03.explanation: Make the transition without contaminating food that is not heated after shaping.

rst-1-week06-q04.objective: Control hand and utensil hygiene and storage in processes without a final heating step.
rst-1-week06-q04.stem: Too much dressed food is prepared and must wait for service. What should be checked?
options: Only utensil-use count
Ignore temperature once finished
Add vinegar to remove expiry limits
Storage method and elapsed time
rst-1-week06-q04.explanation: Maintain food-appropriate temperature and time after mixing and watch for quality changes.

rst-1-week06-q05.objective: Match equipment names to their functions and distinguish heating, hot holding, cooling, and storage.
rst-1-week06-q05.stem: The rice cook prepared only a warmer. What distinction should be checked?
options: Only names differ
Cooking rice versus keeping cooked rice warm
No distinction because functions match
Both make ice
rst-1-week06-q05.explanation: Cooking and hot-holding equipment have different roles. Check purpose.

rst-1-week06-q06.objective: Match equipment names to their functions and distinguish heating, hot holding, cooling, and storage.
rst-1-week06-q06.stem: What guides equipment selection for cooling hot food before storage?
options: Only empty shelf color
Whatever is nearest without checking its name
All refrigeration labels mean the same
Required cooling capacity and suitability for the storage process
rst-1-week06-q06.explanation: Distinguish rapid cooling from cold storage and choose methods meeting process conditions.

rst-1-week06-q07.objective: Relate dishwashing and ingredient-processing equipment to its purpose and safe operation.
rst-1-week06-q07.stem: Dishes leave the washer still dirty. What check is appropriate?
options: Pretreatment, loading, and machine condition
Store them because they passed through
Hide dirt with food
Drying always removes dirt
rst-1-week06-q07.explanation: Check the result, not just machine use, and rewash or inspect as necessary.

rst-1-week06-q08.objective: Check cooking utensil names and purposes to prevent misuse and contamination.
rst-1-week06-q08.stem: Portions of the same dish vary by worker. What utensil check helps?
options: Freely choosing long handles
Only matching plate colors
Sharing the capacity of the assigned serving utensil
Assuming all large utensils are equivalent
rst-1-week06-q08.explanation: Share standard portions and suitable utensils to serve consistent quantities.

rst-1-week07-q01.objective: Measure weight, core temperature, surface temperature, and time using appropriate instruments.
rst-1-week07-q01.stem: The container weighs 200g and the filled total is 650g. What is the ingredient weight?
rst-1-week07-q01.explanation: Subtracting the 200g container from 650g gives 450g of ingredients. Check net weight.

rst-1-week07-q02.objective: Measure weight, core temperature, surface temperature, and time using appropriate instruments.
rst-1-week07-q02.stem: Someone plans to fill core-heating records with a surface-temperature reading. What is appropriate?
options: Recheck using core-measurement equipment and method
Just copy the number
Erase the time and copy it
Change only the instrument name
rst-1-week07-q02.explanation: The targets differ. Do not treat a surface reading as a core check.

rst-1-week07-q03.objective: Anticipate lifting and carrying risks and choose to split loads or seek assistance.
rst-1-week07-q03.stem: There is a heavy pot and a wet passage. What should happen before carrying?
options: Pick it up then run
Fill it because it is heavy
Carry it at once without avoiding water
Clear the route and check manageable quantity and staffing
rst-1-week07-q03.explanation: Check weight, heat, and footing together and split loads or seek help.

rst-1-week07-q04.objective: Anticipate lifting and carrying risks and choose to split loads or seek assistance.
rst-1-week07-q04.stem: Cart loads block forward vision. What comes before departure?
options: Run backward without visibility
Adjust stacking and quantity for safe vision
Stack even higher
Push without alerting others
rst-1-week07-q04.explanation: Avoid overly high stacks and ensure stability and forward visibility.

rst-1-week07-q05.objective: Distinguish safety procedures during use and cleaning and handle blades safely.
rst-1-week07-q05.stem: You will clean equipment whose rotating blade is slowing. What condition is required?
options: Touch it if quiet
Verify power isolation and complete stoppage
Stop the blade using gloves
Spray water while plugged in
rst-1-week07-q05.explanation: Follow equipment procedures, including switching off and unplugging, and work only after complete blade stoppage.

rst-1-week07-q06.objective: Distinguish safety procedures during use and cleaning and handle blades safely.
rst-1-week07-q06.stem: A used knife is placed under a cloth. What is dangerous?
options: Covering it removes the need to communicate its position
Blade direction does not matter on cloth
The next person may touch the unseen blade
Covering it removes the need to return it
rst-1-week07-q06.explanation: Do not leave blades hidden. Wash and return them to dedicated storage.

rst-1-week07-q07.objective: Isolate chipped items or fragments when found and handle chemicals correctly.
rst-1-week07-q07.stem: Glass breaks near food and fragment spread is unknown. What should be done?
options: Pick up visible pieces and use everything
Turn dishes and serve
Separate affected food and utensils and request a check
Assume warming removes fragments
rst-1-week07-q07.explanation: Do not use insufficiently checked items. Confirm affected scope and actions with the responsible person.

rst-1-week07-q08.objective: Inspect fire sources and electrical equipment and choose safe actions without attempting unsafe firefighting.
rst-1-week07-q08.stem: A kitchen fire grows beyond safe extinguishing. What should the initial responder prioritize?
options: Alert others, withdraw, and enable evacuation
Block escape and keep fighting
Proceed farther inside alone
Continue without alerting guests
rst-1-week07-q08.explanation: Fight fire only within safe limits. Withdraw and evacuate when danger increases.

rst-1-week08-q01.objective: Observe food, service, cleanliness, and atmosphere to select improvements.
rst-1-week08-q01.stem: Food is good but temperature and lighting feel uncomfortable. What improvement area matters most?
options: Only ingredient cuts
Atmosphere and comfort
Only payment brands
Only banknotes
rst-1-week08-q01.explanation: QSCA atmosphere includes facilities and the interior environment, with comfort as a foundation.

rst-1-week08-q02.objective: Observe food, service, cleanliness, and atmosphere to select improvements.
rst-1-week08-q02.stem: Portions and plating vary for the same menu item. What should be shared?
options: Standard quantity and plating example
Free quantities for each worker
Only plate prices
Only payment voice volume
rst-1-week08-q02.explanation: Quality includes consistent portions and plating. Share standards.

rst-1-week08-q03.objective: Express welcome and apologies with clean appearance and calm movements.
rst-1-week08-q03.stem: You notice guests arrive but cannot leave your task. What initial action fits service basics?
options: Do not look until finished
Only shout with your back turned
Ask them into the kitchen
Acknowledge them and arrange guidance
rst-1-week08-q03.explanation: Greet or respond to acknowledge them, connect to staff, and manage the waiting situation.

rst-1-week08-q04.objective: Express welcome and apologies with clean appearance and calm movements.
rst-1-week08-q04.stem: You bow apologetically while walking without stopping. What needs improvement?
options: Stop safely, compose posture, and bow politely
Only walk faster
Bow while looking away
Assume a brief neck nod suffices
rst-1-week08-q04.explanation: Basic movements require stopping, composing posture, and a polite purpose-appropriate bow.

rst-1-week08-q05.objective: Check dish contact points and center of gravity to carry food steadily.
rst-1-week08-q05.stem: A tray nearly tilts when a heavy plate is removed. What should be reviewed?
options: Only plate color
Only dish-name pronunciation
Wetting the grip
Stability of arrangement and unloading order
rst-1-week08-q05.explanation: The center of gravity changes during unloading too. Check stable placement and procedures.

rst-1-week08-q06.objective: Check dish contact points and center of gravity to carry food steadily.
rst-1-week08-q06.stem: Someone carries a glass with fingers on its rim. What grip change is appropriate?
options: Grip inside it
Hide the rim under cloth
Hold lower down, avoiding mouth-contact areas
Roll the glass on a plate
rst-1-week08-q06.explanation: Keep the drinking rim clean and hold steadily.

rst-1-week08-q07.objective: Understand basic one-soup, three-dish placement and service order and serve according to restaurant policy.
rst-1-week08-q07.stem: Guests say Japanese seating differs from their wishes. What should the host do?
options: Refuse changes solely on formal hierarchy
Assign status by appearance and force seating
Check wishes against safety and restaurant policy
Leave it without telling the kitchen
rst-1-week08-q07.explanation: Understand seating basics while checking guest wishes and ease of movement.

rst-1-week08-q08.objective: Check cutlery placement without assuming whether dining is finished.
rst-1-week08-q08.stem: Napkin and cutlery suggest completion but food remains. What comes before clearing?
options: Clear silently based only on utensil position
Confirm dining status and wishes
Move food to another table
Always discard everything if guests leave their seats
rst-1-week08-q08.explanation: Placement is a clue. Confirm circumstances and wishes before clearing.

rst-1-week09-q01.objective: Understand round-table seating and serving basics and prevent rotating-table accidents.
rst-1-week09-q01.stem: Someone is serving themselves across the rotating table. How should a new dish be placed?
options: Wait until they finish and alert them
Rotate immediately to make space
Push their hand to stop them
Pass a hot dish overhead
rst-1-week09-q01.explanation: Observe others and avoid collisions during rotation or service.

rst-1-week09-q02.objective: Understand round-table seating and serving basics and prevent rotating-table accidents.
rst-1-week09-q02.stem: A sharing plate retains the previous dish’s flavor. What should be prepared?
options: Someone else’s used plate
All sauces on the same plate
A fresh side plate
Only a glass
rst-1-week09-q02.explanation: Change side plates for different dishes to avoid mixing flavors.

rst-1-week09-q03.objective: Ask preferences and guide families with children, older people, people with disabilities, and others appropriately.
rst-1-week09-q03.stem: A wheelchair user requests movement at their seat. What is needed before assistance?
options: Confirm their wishes and a safe method
Move them based only on wheelchair type
Speak only to a companion
Always require them to leave the chair
rst-1-week09-q03.explanation: Support needs differ. Ask the person and obtain consent before acting.

rst-1-week09-q04.objective: Ask preferences and guide families with children, older people, people with disabilities, and others appropriately.
rst-1-week09-q04.stem: What basic check guides a guest accompanied by an assistance dog?
options: Guide the dog with treats
Leave the person and move the dog separately
Assume it is a pet and refuse entry
Ask which seat and route are convenient for the person
rst-1-week09-q04.explanation: Accommodate assistance-dog access and ask the person what adjustments they need.

rst-1-week09-q05.objective: Serve promptly and accurately convey restaurant storage conditions and time limits for takeout.
rst-1-week09-q05.stem: Transport of a finished cold dish is delayed. What coordination is appropriate?
options: Leave it at room temperature because it is finished
Forget the unrecorded wait
Stack it on hot food
Tell service staff and maintain storage conditions
rst-1-week09-q05.explanation: Continue temperature and time control until service and share the situation among staff.

rst-1-week09-q06.objective: Serve promptly and accurately convey restaurant storage conditions and time limits for takeout.
rst-1-week09-q06.stem: A takeout customer asks the eating time limit, but you have not checked. What should you do?
options: Guess two hours for everything
Say no limit is needed
Check and convey restaurant conditions
Repeat another restaurant’s conditions
rst-1-week09-q06.explanation: Verify restaurant information suited to the food and process; do not personally guarantee unknown conditions.

rst-1-week09-q07.objective: Use basic terms appropriately for the situation and clearly confirm orders and suggestions.
rst-1-week09-q07.stem: What is appropriate after a recommendation is declined?
options: Repeat until ordered
Respect the decision and return to necessary guidance
Add food without asking
Ask other guests why it was declined
rst-1-week09-q07.explanation: Keep recommendations within guest preferences and do not pressure after a refusal.

rst-1-week09-q08.objective: Listen carefully, repeat details for confirmation, and pass on messages politely when the other person’s facial expressions are not visible.
rst-1-week09-q08.stem: What should a reservation-call taker pass to kitchen staff?
options: Only memory
Confirmed date/time, guest count, dishes, and requests
Guesses about unclear details
Only the booker’s name
rst-1-week09-q08.explanation: Record key confirmed telephone details and share them accurately with responsible staff.

rst-1-week10-q01.objective: Check ingredients and preparation processes and refer to the responsible person without giving unverified safety assurances.
rst-1-week10-q01.stem: The dish is unchanged but the sauce supplier changed this month. What is needed for an allergy inquiry?
options: Answer from old memory
Skip checks because the name matches
Assume less sauce is safe
Check current ingredient information after the change
rst-1-week10-q01.explanation: Watch for recipe and ingredient changes and respond using current information and processes.

rst-1-week10-q02.objective: Check ingredients and preparation processes and refer to the responsible person without giving unverified safety assurances.
rst-1-week10-q02.stem: An ingredient-exclusion order was not passed to service staff. What comes before serving?
options: Serve if cooked
Recheck order conditions and the dish’s compliance
Erase the note
Ask guests to check in the kitchen
rst-1-week10-q02.explanation: Share information through service, not only cooking, to deliver the correct dish.

rst-1-week10-q03.objective: Distinguish fermented and distilled alcoholic drinks and perform necessary age and driving checks.
rst-1-week10-q03.stem: One group member will drive. Which order handling is appropriate?
options: Serve one drink at your discretion
Skip checks if a companion orders
Serve alcohol with food
Share that this person must not receive alcohol
rst-1-week10-q03.explanation: Identify drivers and inform ordering and serving staff so they are not served alcohol.

rst-1-week10-q04.objective: Distinguish fermented and distilled alcoholic drinks and perform necessary age and driving checks.
rst-1-week10-q04.stem: An age check shows a customer is under 20. What is appropriate?
options: Always serve with a guardian
Ignore age if food is ordered
Offer available nonalcoholic drinks
Serve alcohol under another name
rst-1-week10-q04.explanation: Do not serve alcohol to under-20s. Politely offer drinks the restaurant can provide.

rst-1-week10-q05.objective: Use the main functions of nutrients and taste differences in basic explanations of dishes.
rst-1-week10-q05.stem: A customer asks about salt content, but verified figures are unavailable. What should you do?
options: Guarantee low salt if it does not taste salty
Avoid taste-based claims and seek verifiable information
Say all vegetable dishes are salt-free
Promise health effects yourself
rst-1-week10-q05.explanation: Taste varies by person. Use verified information for nutrient amounts.

rst-1-week10-q06.objective: Respect religious and dietary differences and specifically confirm foods the customer cannot eat.
rst-1-week10-q06.stem: What is needed when suggesting a dish to someone avoiding animal foods?
options: Check their conditions including stock and seasonings
Visible vegetables mean full compliance
Only hide meat
Choose one option without asking
rst-1-week10-q06.explanation: Animal-derived ingredients may be hidden. Check specific requirements and processes.

rst-1-week10-q07.objective: Respect religious and dietary differences and specifically confirm foods the customer cannot eat.
rst-1-week10-q07.stem: A halal request cannot be met with dedicated utensils. What should be said?
options: Explain accurately what can and cannot be done
Guarantee everything if there is no pork
Hide utensil conditions and accept
Ask other guests about the person’s wishes
rst-1-week10-q07.explanation: Clearly state accommodation limits and checked information without unverified guarantees.

rst-1-week10-q08.objective: Perform checks in order before and after service and hand over unfinished tasks.
rst-1-week10-q08.stem: Reservation numbers change before opening. What coordination is needed?
options: Change seats only, not the kitchen
Prepare for the old count
Update and share kitchen and seating quantities
Do not record the change
rst-1-week10-q08.explanation: Changes affect food, dishes, seating, and staff. Share them among responsible workers.

rst-1-week11-q01.objective: Choose cleaning tools and order suited to the area and check what customers can see.
rst-1-week11-q01.stem: After cleaning, dirt below is visible when sitting. How should checking improve?
options: Check only surfaces seen from above
Include the customer’s viewpoint
Hide the chair from use
Close the seat without authorization
rst-1-week11-q01.explanation: Inspect from actual user positions as well as the worker’s viewpoint.

rst-1-week11-q02.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-week11-q02.stem: A terminal stalls while processing and the guest offers cash too. What comes first?
options: Take cash without checking
Read the card repeatedly
Take both without records
Check payment status to prevent duplicate payment
rst-1-week11-q02.explanation: Verify unclear results through the responsible person or restaurant procedure and avoid duplicate processing.

rst-1-week11-q03.objective: Match amounts and payment methods to prevent duplicate charges and change errors.
rst-1-week11-q03.stem: The bill is 3,200 yen and you receive 5,000 yen. How much change?
rst-1-week11-q03.explanation: 5,000 yen−3,200 yen＝1,800 yen. Check the amount received and change before handing it over.

rst-1-week11-q04.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-week11-q04.stem: A foreign-object complainant does not want a remake. What is appropriate?
options: Always place a new dish unilaterally
Decide charges yourself and end it
Confirm wishes and decide with the responsible person
Discard evidence and pretend nothing happened
rst-1-week11-q04.explanation: Remakes and charges follow customer wishes and restaurant authority.

rst-1-week11-q05.objective: Listen to customers, preserve items and facts, and report accurately to the responsible person.
rst-1-week11-q05.stem: A complaint’s facts are unclear. What is the first response?
options: Listen and pass confirmed information to the responsible person
Declare the guest responsible first
Blame another employee definitively
Leave without hearing it
rst-1-week11-q05.explanation: Understand the issue without assuming causes and refer decisions beyond your authority.

rst-1-week11-q06.objective: Ensure safety, communicate symptoms, request emergency help when necessary, and coordinate within the restaurant.
rst-1-week11-q06.stem: A guest has breathing difficulty and altered consciousness. What is appropriate?
options: Prioritize assistance and emergency calls
Wait until payment ends
Investigate fully alone before calling
Force food on them
rst-1-week11-q06.explanation: Prioritize safety and emergency response, report symptoms and location, and follow instructions.

rst-1-week11-q07.objective: Ensure personal safety before acting according to restaurant roles and evacuation plans.
rst-1-week11-q07.stem: After earthquake shaking stops, what should be checked before evacuation?
options: Only sales
Surrounding damage and safe routes
Only dish counts
Only next booking time
rst-1-week11-q07.explanation: Even after shaking stops, watch for falling and broken objects and guide along verified safe routes.

rst-1-week11-q08.objective: Ensure personal safety before acting according to restaurant roles and evacuation plans.
rst-1-week11-q08.stem: After evacuation a guest wants belongings. What should you do?
options: Allow return one at a time
Return with them unconditionally
Tell them not to return and inform the responsible person
Do not check numbers returning
rst-1-week11-q08.explanation: Do not reenter after fire evacuation and tell guests not to return.

rst-1-week12-q01.objective: Distinguish egg exceptions from bans on raw liver and heat to the center using verified restaurant procedures.
rst-1-week12-q01.stem: When assessing raw-egg exceptions, what is checked besides expiry?
options: Only shell color
Normal eggs without dirt or cracks and prompt handling conditions
Only size
Whether the dish name is short
rst-1-week12-q01.explanation: Do not approve raw use from expiry alone. Check normal egg condition and handling requirements.

rst-1-week12-q02.objective: Distinguish egg exceptions from bans on raw liver and heat to the center using verified restaurant procedures.
rst-1-week12-q02.stem: A guest requests rare beef liver. What should the order taker do?
options: Serve as requested if fresh
Ignore rules if requested
Explain it must be properly heated to the center
Guarantee safety from surface searing
rst-1-week12-q02.explanation: Do not serve beef liver raw. Follow verified heating processes without changing them solely at a guest’s request.

rst-1-week12-q03.objective: Explain hygiene index terms by their roles in causes, prevention, checks, and records.
rst-1-week12-q03.stem: What question clarifies a new worker’s “temperature seems wrong” report?
options: Only whether it feels unusual
Only whether others share that impression
What was measured, with which instrument, when, against which standard
End the report if nothing looks wrong
rst-1-week12-q03.explanation: Clarifying target, instrument, time, and standard supports sound decisions and records.

rst-1-week12-q04.objective: Explain hygiene index terms by their roles in causes, prevention, checks, and records.
rst-1-week12-q04.stem: How are norovirus and Anisakis classified?
options: Virus and parasite
Both bacteria
Both detergents
Both metal objects
rst-1-week12-q04.explanation: Distinguish hazard categories and connect terms to necessary controls.

rst-1-week12-q05.objective: Connect index names with actual features and uses and distinguish homophones and alternative names.
rst-1-week12-q05.stem: You hear “prepare kaki” but the ingredient category is unclear. What is appropriate?
options: Treat identical sounds as identical food
Use your preferred one
Chop first, check later
Check instructions and actual items: persimmon or oyster
rst-1-week12-q05.explanation: The same reading can mean different foods. Match category and item before working.

rst-1-week12-q06.objective: Connect index names with actual features and uses and distinguish homophones and alternative names.
rst-1-week12-q06.stem: The index term “riburiisu” is unclear. What is appropriate?
options: Compare the text’s beef cut with the usual rib roast term
Replace it with a fish name
Order all similar sounds as the same item
Start using without checking
rst-1-week12-q06.explanation: For suspected index errors, compare body text and actual items rather than guessing a different food.

rst-1-week12-q07.objective: Select service-index terms and distinguish customer-facing expressions from kitchen work terminology.
rst-1-week12-q07.stem: What does the kitchen instruction “coordinate the main dishes for the same table” mean?
options: Clear only the top seat
Move all drinks to payment
Mix plates across tables
Coordinate main-dish service for one table
rst-1-week12-q07.explanation: Same table identifies the group; main dish is a meal role. Understand internal terms and use clear language with guests.

rst-1-week12-q08.objective: Select service-index terms and distinguish customer-facing expressions from kitchen work terminology.
rst-1-week12-q08.stem: After learning halal, vegan, and allergy terms, what is correct?
options: Treat all as the same restriction
Check each meaning and the individual’s conditions
Decide solely from nationality
Knowing terms removes ingredient checks
rst-1-week12-q08.explanation: Do not decide from terms alone. Understand different backgrounds and specific needs and check ingredients and processes.

rst-2-q001.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q001.stem: Inventory sheets use kg but staff count bags. What correction is appropriate?
options: Enter bags directly under kg
Reuse last month’s figures
Align conversion units and verify actual counts and calculations
Delete the unit field
rst-2-q001.explanation: Mismatched units distort inventory value and costs. Convert using specifications and verify actual quantities.

rst-2-q002.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q002.stem: Glove-changing timing varies among employees. What improvement applies?
options: Same glove type removes checking change conditions
Change only at fixed times, not after dirt or task changes
Teach changing after task changes and contamination together with handwashing
Replace pre-glove handwashing with strict glove changes
rst-2-q002.explanation: Gloves also become contaminated. Teach and check changing and handwashing as one procedure.

rst-2-q003.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q003.stem: Sales are 500,000 yen and cost of goods is 150,000 yen. What is the cost ratio?
rst-2-q003.explanation: Cost ratio equals cost of goods÷sales×100. 150,000÷500,000×100＝30%.

rst-2-q004.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q004.stem: Dishwasher dirt remains in the same places. What should be checked first?
options: Remove only dirty dishes and wait for scheduled maintenance
Nozzles, racks, detergent supply, and operating conditions
Extend time without checking nozzles or loading
Exclude detergent and racks if temperature looks normal
rst-2-q004.explanation: Investigate equipment condition, loading, chemical supply, and temperature conditions.

rst-2-q005.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q005.stem: Insects increase near outdoor waste storage. What should the manager do?
options: Spray more only inside the kitchen
Ignore it because it is outside
Spray with food exposed
Investigate and improve breeding sources and entry routes
rst-2-q005.explanation: Surroundings affect pest entry. Combine source control and exclusion while preventing food contamination.

rst-2-q006.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q006.stem: Waste stays longer in the kitchen after collection timing changes. What improvement applies?
options: Mix it into food refrigerators
Leave bags open
Review storage and removal plans
Keep procedures unchanged
rst-2-q006.explanation: Adjust temporary storage and removal to collection changes to prevent contamination and pests.

rst-2-q007.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q007.stem: Cutting only service time to increase sales raises complaints. What management decision is appropriate?
options: Exclude complaints and keep cutting
Maintain QSC and review process waste
Remove service-quality goals
Only raise prices
rst-2-q007.explanation: Improve efficiency without sacrificing required quality, service, and cleanliness. Do not judge from sales alone.

rst-2-q008.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q008.stem: To reduce vegetable preparation, cutting begins without checking damaged parts. What instruction applies?
options: Evaluate only cutting speed
Restore freshness checks and proper preparation to the process
Check everything after cooking
Reading names is enough
rst-2-q008.explanation: Ingredient condition affects finished food. Efficiency must not remove necessary freshness and quality checks.

rst-2-q009.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q009.stem: Food meets standards but attitude complaints increase. What should the manager do?
options: Nothing because food is good
Remove complaining guests from records
Only discount everything
Observe service and give specific coaching
rst-2-q009.explanation: Service needs checks separately from food. Improve by observing actual attitudes and responses.

rst-2-q010.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q010.stem: A fluoropolymer-coated pan surface deteriorates easily. What care should be reviewed?
options: Scrub hard with steel wool
Dry-heat then immediately add cold water
Widen damage with metal spatulas
Use a soft sponge and avoid rapid cooling
rst-2-q010.explanation: Use cleaning suited to the coating and consider temperature changes. Abrasion and thermal shock cause damage.

rst-2-q011.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q011.stem: Knife disinfection records are normal but grease remains. What should be investigated first?
options: Only extend disinfectant contact time without checking cleaning
Leave dirt to washer discretion if records meet standards
Whether washing removed the dirt
Add disinfectant before cleaning and recheck only records
rst-2-q011.explanation: Residual dirt may impair disinfection. Start with actual washing and rinsing practices.

rst-2-q012.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q012.stem: Hot-soup carrying collisions recur at one location. What prevents recurrence?
options: Make staff run until accustomed
Post a warning but leave obstacles
Review and communicate routes, movement flows, and carrying methods
Only use larger pots to reduce trips
rst-2-q012.explanation: Review obstacles, routes, visibility, and carrying procedures together to reduce inherent work risks.

rst-2-q013.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q013.stem: Cleaning results vary greatly by person. What belongs in the manual?
options: Targets, tools, methods, frequency, and finish standards
Only more names and end times, leaving methods and standards to individuals
Only uniform duration, omitting scope and finish checks
Only detergent names, without scope or tool use
rst-2-q013.explanation: Share specific procedures and standards and check actual results on site.

rst-2-q014.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q014.stem: Why keep hygiene records on normal days too?
options: To erase responsibility even if problems occur
To verify the history of implemented controls
To guarantee safety through record quantity
To change values freely later
rst-2-q014.explanation: Records show checks and history and help identify trends and investigate abnormalities. They do not automatically guarantee safety.

rst-2-q015.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q015.stem: Spare chairs are in an evacuation passage. What should the manager instruct?
options: Move them only during fire
Cover them with cloth
Hide evacuation signs
Clear the passage and review storage and daily checks
rst-2-q015.explanation: Keep evacuation routes clear routinely. Do not leave obstacles assuming they can be moved in emergencies.

rst-2-q016.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q016.stem: The ventilation fan stops in a gas-equipped kitchen. What should be instructed?
options: Continue normal flames if no odor
Assume a slightly open window suffices without checking ventilation
Stop use and confirm safe ventilation and equipment response
Lower heat and continue until recovery
