rst-2-q016.explanation: Poor ventilation can cause carbon monoxide poisoning. Odor does not establish safety.

rst-2-q017.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q017.stem: Alcohol disinfection of counters has inconsistent effects. What should be checked?
options: Drying after washing and product-use conditions
Only increase quantity without checking moisture
Judge effects only by elapsed work hours
Assume identical effects regardless of dirt or wetness
rst-2-q017.explanation: Moisture, dirt, and application matter. Check washing, drying, and labeled conditions.

rst-2-q018.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q018.stem: New guests come but few return. What improvement focus applies?
options: Only more advertising, ignoring existing guests
Prioritize new guests and make regulars wait
Remove quality goals
Check QSC and guest experience and develop relationships
rst-2-q018.explanation: Return visits depend on satisfaction and relationships; acquisition alone cannot fix declining regulars.

rst-2-q019.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q019.stem: A worker promises a refund before checking complaint facts. What improvement is needed?
options: Clarify authority and reporting standards for consistent responses
Allow unlimited promises by all staff
Ignore every complaint
Prohibit apologies
rst-2-q019.explanation: Apologize and check facts; compensation must follow authority and restaurant policy.

rst-2-q020.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q020.stem: A new worker uses internal abbreviations with guests. What coaching applies?
options: Confirm with official product names guests understand
Only fix pronunciation
Make every guest learn abbreviations
Remove order confirmation
rst-2-q020.explanation: Internal terms may not communicate meaning. Use full names to confirm orders without confusion.

rst-2-q021.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q021.stem: Hot-holding equipment failed and the stop time is unknown. How should you decide?
options: Serve everything if it feels warm
Fill records and serve
Investigate temperature and time and withhold service until safety is confirmed
Skip history checks after reheating
rst-2-q021.explanation: Time and temperature outside control are needed. Touch and reheating alone cannot prove safety.

rst-2-q022.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q022.stem: Only a food-hygiene officer’s name is displayed, with no site checks. What improvement is necessary?
options: Clarify the role and actual hygiene activities
Only enlarge the sign
Only increase names on paper
Leave everything to suppliers
rst-2-q022.explanation: Assigning a role alone does not implement hygiene. Connect it to planning, guidance, and checks.

rst-2-q023.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q023.stem: A recall notice covers the ingredient lot. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Identify affected items, stop use, and isolate
Discount and use them up
Decide heating excludes them
Discard slips to conceal identity
rst-2-q023.explanation: Identify and isolate recalled items and establish what was served. Do not continue use unilaterally.

rst-2-q024.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q024.stem: A drinking group plans to change drivers midway. What should you do?
options: Check only the original driver
Serve the replacement alcohol first
Recheck planned drivers and control alcohol service
Guarantee driving is possible after eating
rst-2-q024.explanation: Identify drivers when plans change too. Initial checks alone do not justify continued alcohol service.

rst-2-q025.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q025.stem: A trainee heard an explanation but cannot do the task. What OJT is appropriate?
options: Demonstrate, let them perform, and observe
Give documents and stop checking
Assume one explanation enables independence
Reassign without checking failure reasons
rst-2-q025.explanation: Practical skills require demonstration, practice, observation, and follow-up; explanations alone do not verify learning.

rst-2-q026.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q026.stem: Unopened shelf-life labeling is used unchanged for opened sauce. What improvement applies?
options: Set and verify post-opening storage and use limits
Use unconditionally until the printed date
Extend by transferring containers
Extend daily by tasting alone
rst-2-q026.explanation: Printed dates generally assume specified unopened conditions. Manage opened products separately.

rst-2-q027.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q027.stem: All employees gather around an ill guest. What needs improvement?
options: Everyone asks the same questions
Give one manager every task
Prioritize normal service
Allocate calling, assistance, and other guests’ safety
rst-2-q027.explanation: Assign roles for simultaneous communication and support to reduce confusion.

rst-2-q028.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q028.stem: Cooked meat curls and disrupts plating. What preparation should be considered?
options: Apply thick sugar
Locate connective tissue and make appropriate cuts
Leave meat overnight at room temperature
Only change plate size
rst-2-q028.explanation: Connective tissue between lean and fat contracts on heating. Appropriate scoring helps stabilize shape.

rst-2-q029.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q029.stem: The floor is wet near a family with children. What is the manager’s priority?
options: Ignore because parents watch
Wait until seating fills
Place belongings on the slippery area
Warn against entry and remove moisture promptly
rst-2-q029.explanation: Reduce fall risks for all ages. Remove wetness and ensure safe routes rather than relying only on signs.

rst-2-q030.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q030.stem: Some stir-fry ingredients are hard while others overcook. What improvement applies?
options: Add all at the end
Review addition order for cooking needs
Only mix after plating
Only lower plate temperature
rst-2-q030.explanation: Ingredients heat differently. Adjust cuts, order, and heating times.

rst-2-q031.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q031.stem: A tough connective-tissue-rich beef cut is quickly grilled and draws complaints. What improvement applies?
options: Only change plates
Review cut characteristics and cooking-method pairing
Raise price to signal quality
Keep heating the same and delay serving
rst-2-q031.explanation: Choose cuts and methods suited to the dish. Appearance and price do not solve toughness.

rst-2-q032.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q032.stem: How should management investigate why regulars stopped coming?
options: Do not investigate if new guests come
Publish regulars’ information
Decide solely from discount rates
Check service/quality changes and customer feedback
rst-2-q032.explanation: Use visit patterns and feedback to assess satisfaction while protecting personal information.

rst-2-q033.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q033.stem: A worker says freezing once removes all hazards. What instruction applies?
options: Agree frozen food is sterile
Teach that freezing, heating, and other controls differ by hazard
Remove post-thaw temperature management
Thaw everything at room temperature
rst-2-q033.explanation: Freezing is not universal disinfection. Controls must suit microbial, parasitic, and chemical hazards.

rst-2-q034.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q034.stem: A trainee uses correct greetings too quietly to be heard. What improvement applies?
options: Only repeat memorization
Use silent bows only
Ignore guest reactions
Practice volume, expression, and eye contact
rst-2-q034.explanation: Effective service involves voice, expression, and posture as well as words. Practice situation-appropriate delivery.

rst-2-q035.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q035.stem: A new dish starts but the hygiene plan still covers old menus. What should the manager do?
options: Only add its name
Check new-process hazards and revise the plan
Wait for problems
Rely only on staff experience
rst-2-q035.explanation: Ingredients and processes change hazards and controls. Also check record forms and staff communication.

rst-2-q036.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q036.stem: Water-quality checks for storage equipment are overdue. What should be done?
options: Clear water needs no testing
Boiling removes records
Identify required inspections and arrange action
Backdate the planned check
rst-2-q036.explanation: Appearance alone cannot verify safety. Perform checks and record management appropriate to the equipment category.

rst-2-q037.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q037.stem: A refrigerator gasket is damaged. What should be checked?
options: Only visible closure, omitting sealing and temperature
Assume a lower setting solves damage
Wipe and continue until the next check without assessing temperature
Effects on sealing/temperature and repair needs
rst-2-q037.explanation: Gasket faults affect sealing and cleanability. Check temperature and hygiene and correct equipment defects.

rst-2-q038.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q038.stem: Actual cost exceeds theoretical cost. What initial investigation is appropriate?
options: Check portions, waste, inventory, and receiving
Blame only selling prices
Lower cost records
Bill suppliers for the gap without evidence
rst-2-q038.explanation: Overportioning, waste, and count or recording errors can cause differences. Check multiple factors.

rst-2-q039.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q039.stem: ABC analysis identifies low-selling dishes. What next decision is appropriate?
options: Immediately remove all based only on quantity
Order large amounts only of slow sellers
Check sales contribution and role when considering revisions
Mistake results for guest counts
rst-2-q039.explanation: ABC informs revisions. Consider profit, customer segments, and menu roles too.

rst-2-q040.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q040.stem: What matters in training staff making unheated dressed dishes?
options: Hand/utensil hygiene and finished-food storage
Saying a final heating step always occurs
Saying bare hands need no washing
Setting expiry only by appearance
rst-2-q040.explanation: Unheated processes lack later cooking after contamination. Control hands, utensils, and refrigeration reliably.

rst-2-q041.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q041.stem: Staff clean only visible seating areas. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Dim lights to hide dirt
Skip cleaning when few guests
Substitute stronger fragrance
Share cleanliness standards including fixtures and blind spots
rst-2-q041.explanation: Define scope and finish standards for consistent cleanliness. Concealment and fragrance cannot replace cleaning.

rst-2-q042.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q042.stem: A worker memorized service terms but replies with stock phrases without listening. What instruction applies?
options: Only increase phrase count
Practice the purpose of terms and checking requests
Interrupt to make them speak faster
Require only identical emotionless responses
rst-2-q042.explanation: Service terms enable communication. Understand situations and requests and connect them to action.

rst-2-q043.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q043.stem: Two core thermometers give different readings on the same sample. What should the manager decide?
options: Check accuracy and affected measurements
Choose only the convenient high value
Keep both unconditionally
Change all past records to averages
rst-2-q043.explanation: Accuracy faults mislead cooking decisions. Inspect/calibrate, consider stopping use, and assess prior measurements.

rst-2-q044.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q044.stem: Staff use a new payment terminal differently on launch day. What should the manager do?
options: Watch sales and leave operation to staff
Prevent result checks
Simply charge again after failure
Train procedures including cancellations and abnormalities
rst-2-q044.explanation: Share handling of normal payments, duplicates, and cancellations to prevent payment incidents.

rst-2-q045.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q045.stem: Nearby event days repeatedly cause stockouts. What ordering improvement applies?
options: Fix identical daily quantities
Reflect past results and events in forecasts
Increase every item without limit
Keep no stockout records
rst-2-q045.explanation: Forecast using weekdays, recent trends, and local events, adjusting quantities while avoiding excess stock.

rst-2-q046.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q046.stem: A quiet-period discount begins. What evaluation is appropriate?
options: Declare success from discount count alone
Check guest count, profit, and effects on other periods
Do not record sales reductions
Lower every period without comparison
rst-2-q046.explanation: Assess discount costs, profit, and demand shifts as well as attraction.

rst-2-q047.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q047.stem: A trainee does not know wheelchair-accessible seating. What comes before opening?
options: Check routes/seating conditions and share guidance
Find furniture only after arrival
Refuse all wheelchair guests
Let only companions choose
rst-2-q047.explanation: Know accessible seats and routes in advance and prepare guidance based on the person’s wishes.

rst-2-q048.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q048.stem: After outsourcing pest control, what must the restaurant do?
options: Stop routine checks because a contract exists
Check results and continue entry/breeding prevention
Do not tell staff chemical locations
Skip food protection
rst-2-q048.explanation: Outsourcing does not remove routine hygiene. Continue reviewing results and facility/waste improvements.

rst-2-q049.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q049.stem: Fire checks find a deteriorated gas hose. What response applies?
options: Bend it out of sight
Mark only the form normal
Verify safe use and arrange proper replacement
Use until it burns
rst-2-q049.explanation: Deterioration risks leaks and fire. Prioritize safety and correct according to equipment procedures.

rst-2-q050.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q050.stem: Health forms are normal but a worker reports vomiting. What takes priority?
options: Continue because records are normal
Delay reporting until shift end
Stop food handling and check circumstances and impact
Only add gloves
rst-2-q050.explanation: Respond to current symptoms; morning forms do not justify continued food handling.

rst-2-q051.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q051.stem: Gross profit is 180,000 yen and total labor is 60 hours. What is labor-hour productivity?
options: 300 yen/hour
3,000 yen/hour
6,000 yen/hour
rst-2-q051.explanation: Here, labor-hour productivity equals gross profit÷total labor hours. 180,000÷60＝3,000 yen/hour.

rst-2-q052.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q052.stem: Raw-meat preparation and cooked-food plating alternate on one counter. What is the priority?
options: Set work separation and washing/disinfection transition procedures
Short raw work permits skipping transition cleaning
Only label areas without treating contact surfaces
Place small cooked batches directly after meat work
rst-2-q052.explanation: Shared facilities require zone, time, utensil separation and transition control; labels alone do not prevent contamination.

rst-2-q053.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q053.stem: A trainee uses the old dilution for a new disinfectant. How should they be instructed?
options: Match concentration by color
Check the new product label and conditions
All chemicals use the same ratio
Stronger is better, use concentrate
rst-2-q053.explanation: Concentration, contact time, and purposes differ by product. Do not transfer old procedures unconditionally.

rst-2-q054.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q054.stem: Cutting boards dry pressed against a wall. What instruction applies?
options: Stack wet
Store hygienically so all surfaces dry
Stand on a dirty floor
Only shave surfaces before use
rst-2-q054.explanation: Drying and storage after cleaning/disinfection are part of hygiene. Review placement leaving moisture.

rst-2-q055.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q055.stem: Hot dishes cannot be served immediately after opening. What improvement applies?
options: Test equipment on the first guest daily
Assign preparation only after orders
Include startup time in preparation plans
Always maximize settings
rst-2-q055.explanation: Know readiness time and prepare to meet quality standards at opening.

rst-2-q056.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q056.stem: A mixer blade nearly moves during cleaning. What should the manager do?
options: Recheck stopping and restart-prevention procedures
Blame only the cleaner
Increase speed for cleaning
Allow running with thicker gloves
rst-2-q056.explanation: Hazardous cleaning requires measures such as stopping. Protective gear alone may not prevent entanglement.

rst-2-q057.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q057.stem: A refrigerator shows weekly temperature faults. How should records be used?
options: Repeat the same report only
Delete abnormal records
Analyze times and usage and prevent recurrence
Keep normal days only
rst-2-q057.explanation: Investigate repeated faults such as doors, loading, and equipment, then confirm corrective effectiveness.

rst-2-q058.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q058.stem: Frying oil contains many crumbs. What counters deterioration?
options: Stop checking after adding fresh oil
Remove crumbs and inspect condition
Dry-heat strongly for a long time
Store in direct sun
rst-2-q058.explanation: Impurities, prolonged heating, and light affect oil. Topping up does not remove the need for checks.

rst-2-q059.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q059.stem: Plating shifts change without clean-utensil handover. What improvement applies?
options: Only ban changes
Rely on memory
Set utensil, hand, and storage checks
Only inspect appearance
rst-2-q059.explanation: Final-step contamination may not be removed by later heating. Define hygiene checks at handover.

rst-2-q060.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q060.stem: A restaurant boils soba and udon in one pot and gets a soba-allergy inquiry. What instruction applies?
options: Say no soba because none is visible in udon
Guarantee safety if noodles are separate
Give accurate information including shared equipment
Let the receiving staff member decide alone
rst-2-q060.explanation: Shared-equipment contact matters as well as ingredients. Do not give uncertain safety guarantees.

rst-2-q061.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q061.stem: A worker says all domestic beef can be labeled wagyu. What response applies?
options: Accept all domestic beef as wagyu
Decide by fat only
Label by price only
Have them check origin versus breed categories
rst-2-q061.explanation: Domestic concerns origin; wagyu concerns breed and related classification. Base labels on sourcing information.

rst-2-q062.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q062.stem: Fish eyes, gills, and firmness differ from standards at delivery. What should the manager do?
options: Assess acceptance against specifications and freshness standards
Always accept because cheap
Accept unconditionally because it will be cooked
Remove heads to hide it
rst-2-q062.explanation: Check freshness and quality at receiving. Low price or planned heating does not justify unconditional acceptance.

rst-2-q063.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q063.stem: What matters when a manager receives a foreign-object report?
options: Discard the item first
Assume the guest is mistaken
Check health effects, the item, and service history
Continue serving the same dish unconditionally
rst-2-q063.explanation: Check guest safety, preserve evidence, and establish scope for investigation and prevention.

rst-2-q064.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q064.stem: Daily sales are 240,000 yen with 200 guests. What is spending per guest?
options: 240 yen
rst-2-q064.explanation: Average spend equals sales÷guest count. 240,000÷200＝1,200 yen, not multiplication by guests.

rst-2-q065.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q065.stem: Service order varies by worker and inconveniences a group. What improvement applies?
options: Always serve whatever finishes first
Order by plate size
Check and share meal format and service standards
Wait for complaints to check
rst-2-q065.explanation: Kitchen and floor staff share progress according to meal format and service standards for consistency.

rst-2-q066.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q066.stem: Arrival order is followed but short-life ingredients remain. What needs review?
options: Use only arrival dates, ignoring expiry differences
Use costly items first to prevent expiry
Group by supplier without expiry-order checks
Use order accounting for lots and expiry dates
rst-2-q066.explanation: Track expiry as well as arrival order to prevent waste and expiry within usable limits.

rst-2-q067.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q067.stem: A worker discusses a regular’s preferences before other guests. What instruction applies?
options: Publish all for customer management
Post it for promotion
Share contact details without consent
Confirm discreetly only as needed and handle information carefully
rst-2-q067.explanation: Even preference-based service must avoid unnecessary disclosure of personal information.

rst-2-q068.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q068.stem: The ice scoop is buried in ice. What improvement applies?
options: Take ice directly by hand
Store hygienically so its handle does not contaminate ice
Put it on the floor
Use it for waste too
rst-2-q068.explanation: Store dedicated utensils cleanly so hand-contact handles do not contaminate ice.

rst-2-q069.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q069.stem: Oven cleaning is requested immediately after cooking. What instruction applies?
options: Put bare hands in hot interiors
Bring the face close despite steam
Rush without safety checks
Follow manual safety steps including cooling and power shutdown
rst-2-q069.explanation: Hot interiors and steam risk burns. Use equipment-specific stopping, cooling, and cleaning steps.

rst-2-q070.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q070.stem: Trainee skill practice is inserted into a busy period without explanation. What improvement applies?
options: Set goals and time for focused practice
Assume busyness teaches without instruction
Increase work without training details
Give full responsibility and stop observing
rst-2-q070.explanation: Plan clear purposes and stages in conditions allowing demonstration, practice, and checking.

rst-2-q071.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q071.stem: Floor-cleaning records exist but food debris collects under equipment. What improvement applies?
options: Only increase completion records without changing cleaning
Specify scope and checking methods
Tighten visible floors but exclude equipment undersides
Only replace staff without sharing scope
rst-2-q071.explanation: Records alone do not show effectiveness. Include blind spots and verify results.

rst-2-q072.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q072.stem: Order is 8kg, delivery note 10kg, and actual goods 8kg. What should happen at receipt?
options: Look only at goods and sign for 10kg
Do nothing because nothing is missing
Compare all three and check the note discrepancy
Record the 2kg gap as waste
rst-2-q072.explanation: Match order, delivery note, and goods. Correct invoice-quantity errors even when goods match the order.

rst-2-q073.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q073.stem: Guests complain about detergent odor during seating-area cleaning. What should be reviewed?
options: Eliminate all cleaning
Add fragrance
Chemical use, cleaning timing, and movement routes
Silently move guests
rst-2-q073.explanation: Ensure hygiene while checking use conditions and customer effects for appropriate methods and timing.

rst-2-q074.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
options: Whether the worker performs independently to standard
Completion based only on attendance
Passing from reciting materials without observation
Success based only on trainer time spent
rst-2-q074.explanation: Verify understanding and practical ability and retrain where needed.

rst-2-q075.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q075.stem: A supplier changes seasoning formulation. What comes before service?
options: Update allergen information and internal materials
Keep documents if taste matches
Use only old labels
Guess answers only for inquiring guests
rst-2-q075.explanation: Formulation changes can affect allergens. Check specifications and update kitchen and service information.

rst-2-q076.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q076.stem: Meat thawing juice flows onto salad vegetables. What should be instructed?
options: Replate vegetables and use
Ignore invisible juice
Wait until next delivery to report
Separate affected foods and improve thawing locations and containers
rst-2-q076.explanation: Assess food suspected of cross-contamination and correct the process allowing runoff.

rst-2-q077.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q077.stem: A trainee cannot work without asking each next step. What does the cooking plan need?
options: Only dish names
Photos without explanation
Only experienced workers’ verbal directions
Clear purposes, process order, utensils, and safety cautions
rst-2-q077.explanation: Plans and manuals clarify what and why to align quality and safety.

rst-2-q078.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q078.stem: Portions vary after a scale is moved. What response applies?
options: Check setup and accuracy
Portion without reading
Use it tilted
Increase every portion
rst-2-q078.explanation: Measuring devices are affected by setup and vibration. Verify correct weighing after movement.

rst-2-q079.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q079.stem: Daily hygiene checks stop when one worker is absent. What management improvement applies?
options: Assign and train substitutes and check methods
Treat absence blanks as normal
Pretend checks occurred the next day
Cancel all leave
rst-2-q079.explanation: Avoid reliance on one individual. Establish backup coverage and record methods.

rst-2-q080.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q080.stem: Mud remains at vegetable bases after washing. What improvement applies?
options: Leave all in the same water for a long time
Only dry-wipe surfaces
Chop with mud remaining
Spread the base, wash carefully, and finish with running-water rinsing
rst-2-q080.explanation: Focus on dirt-retaining areas such as leaf bases. Chopping to hide dirt is not a control.

rst-2-q081.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q081.stem: The dishwasher ran out of detergent but some dishes look clean. What response applies?
options: Use clean-looking dishes unconditionally
Only replace the detergent container
Separate affected dishes, restore conditions, and reprocess
Increase recorded stock
rst-2-q081.explanation: Identify the scope missing required conditions. Do not judge cleanliness by appearance alone; reprocess.

rst-2-q082.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q082.stem: A manager wants fewer checks because no food-poisoning complaints occurred. What is appropriate?
options: Stop all checks until complaints
Verify preventive controls beyond complaint presence
Add paperwork but stop site checks
Let regulars judge safety
rst-2-q082.explanation: Hygiene prevents harm. No complaints alone cannot establish hazards or control effectiveness.

rst-2-q083.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q083.stem: Cooking results differ by worker despite one recipe. What should be checked?
options: Shared batch quantities, heating conditions, and finish standards
Only align plating, leaving cooking to individuals
Skip observation because recipes were distributed
Assume equal experience means identical methods
rst-2-q083.explanation: Align conditions and finished standards and observe implementation to reduce variation.

rst-2-q084.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q084.stem: Which explanation is appropriate for a new traditional-vegetable dish?
options: Regional names mean identical taste
Check origin, variety, and traits and apply them in cooking
Traditional vegetables need no washing
Use identical heating despite different shapes
rst-2-q084.explanation: Understand local food culture and ingredient traits. Names alone do not determine quality or safety.

rst-2-q085.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q085.stem: Web-only booking makes phone users struggle. What response applies?
options: Refuse everyone unable to use it
Ignore inquiries
Count bookings twice
Consider booking methods for the customer base
rst-2-q085.explanation: Balance digital convenience with user circumstances, considering telephone channels and centralized booking management.

rst-2-q086.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q086.stem: Large-print menus exist but staff do not know their location. What improvement is needed?
options: Nothing because prepared
Discard unused
Share storage location and guidance
Wait for guests to find them
rst-2-q086.explanation: Providing materials is not enough. Communicate and organize actual availability when needed.

rst-2-q087.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q087.stem: Water is cut off and handwashing water is insufficient. What should the manager decide?
options: Continue all tasks with gloves only
Verify hygienic continuation conditions and stop service if necessary
Wipe hands with drinking ice
Prepare normal records in advance
rst-2-q087.explanation: Conditions for safe handling and cleaning are lost. Do not continue without verifying effective alternatives.

rst-2-q088.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q088.stem: A disaster roster exists but trainees do not know their roles. What is appropriate?
options: Explain roles and verify through drills
Keep the paper stored
Discuss only after disaster
Evacuate experienced staff only
rst-2-q088.explanation: Emergency plans need communication and drills for execution; documents alone are insufficient.

rst-2-q089.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q089.stem: Meat preparation and raw-vegetable washing cause splashing simultaneously. What improvement applies?
options: Separate locations or times to prevent spray
Just speed meat work and continue together
Use affected vegetables unchecked once splashing is invisible
Only color-code tools without changing splash or routes
rst-2-q089.explanation: Arrange work to prevent cross-contamination through hands, utensils, and splashed water.

rst-2-q090.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q090.stem: Service order becomes confused only at peak times. What should the manager do?
options: First-ready workers win
Skip all order checks
Hide late orders
Coordinate kitchen/floor handover and priorities
rst-2-q090.explanation: Busy periods require interdepartmental coordination and progress control to reduce missed or misordered service.

rst-2-q091.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q091.stem: Required stock until next delivery is 18 bags, usable stock is 7, and no other deliveries are planned. How many to order?
options: 25 bags
18 bags
7 bags
11 bags
rst-2-q091.explanation: Subtract usable stock:18−7＝11 bags. Do not add safety stock beyond the example’s conditions.

rst-2-q092.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q092.stem: A dull knife makes staff cut with excessive force. What improvement applies?
options: Teach more force
Increase speed without watching
Maintain the blade for its use and check safe cutting
Lift slippery food high by hand
rst-2-q092.explanation: Combine tool maintenance with safe handling. Excessive force and unstable posture cause cuts.

rst-2-q093.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q093.stem: Only the previous worker knows reservation guests’ preferences. What improvement applies?
options: Display all data in seating areas
Store only on a personal phone
Set a proper method to share necessary information
Force private calls to the former worker each time
rst-2-q093.explanation: Manage required customer information under restaurant rules for consistent handovers.

rst-2-q094.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q094.stem: Opening stock is 50,000 yen, purchases200,000, closing stock70,000. What is actual cost?
rst-2-q094.explanation: 50,000＋200,000−70,000＝180,000 yen. Purchases alone do not show the period’s usage cost.

rst-2-q095.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q095.stem: Someone proposes one thawing method for all frozen food. What decision applies?
options: Choose according to food use and product labels
Leave raw-consumption foods at room temperature too
Always fully thaw coated semifinished products
Return thawing juice to all food
rst-2-q095.explanation: Methods differ by raw-consumption and semifinished products. Check instructions and hygiene to set processes.

rst-2-q096.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q096.stem: Opening checklists are marked but change is short. What should be reviewed?
options: Actual checks and completion criteria
Treat all marks as completion
Copy yesterday’s change without checking today
Only add items without defining completion
rst-2-q096.explanation: Verify actual readiness, not just marks. Clarify required amounts and shortage responses.

rst-2-q097.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q097.stem: A worker carries heavy boxes and cannot see their feet. What management improvement is appropriate?
options: Use the current practice as the standard because they can lift it
Reduce passage lighting
Increase boxes carried at once
Include split loads or carts in procedures
rst-2-q097.explanation: Assess falls from visibility and balance as well as weight, and improve carrying methods and passages.

rst-2-q098.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q098.stem: A thermometer was inspected but results were not recorded. What is needed?
options: Rely only on the inspector’s memory
Rewrite all readings as standard values
Keep traceable inspection conditions, results, and actions
Remove thermometer identification
rst-2-q098.explanation: Keep identification and inspection history to establish reliability and trace effects of defects.

rst-2-q099.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q099.stem: Hygiene records are always reviewed together at month end. What improvement applies?
options: Set review frequency allowing prompt abnormality response
Change all abnormalities to normal
Print more forms every half year
Do not contact the worksite
rst-2-q099.explanation: Review must allow timely detection and correction; month-end signatures alone delay response.

rst-2-q100.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q100.stem: An applicant’s preferred hours differ from restaurant needs. What is appropriate?
options: Set shifts without telling them
Assume availability from the résumé alone
Check both parties’ conditions and possible adjustments
Explain conditions only after hiring
rst-2-q100.explanation: Check desired roles, hours, rules, and requests to reduce mismatched conditions.

rst-2-q101.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q101.stem: Sales are 360,000 yen and total labor is 60 hours. What are sales per labor hour?
options: 60,000 yen/hour
216,000 yen/hour
6,000 yen/hour
600 yen/hour
rst-2-q101.explanation: Sales per labor hour equal sales÷total labor hours.360,000÷60＝6,000 yen/hour.

rst-2-q102.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q102.stem: Gross profit is 400,000 yen and labor cost160,000 yen. What is the labor distribution ratio?
rst-2-q102.explanation: Labor distribution ratio equals labor cost÷gross profit×100. 160,000÷400,000×100＝40%.

rst-2-q103.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q103.stem: There are 240 guests and48 total labor hours. How many guests are served per labor hour?
options: 48 guests/hour
5 guests/hour
50 guests/hour
192 guests/hour
rst-2-q103.explanation: Guests per labor hour equal guest count÷total labor hours.240÷48＝5 guests/hour.

rst-2-q104.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q104.stem: Opened boxes are counted only as “1 box” at closing inventory. What improvement applies?
options: Count empty boxes as1 box too
Use last year’s stock
Count remaining quantities accurately and align units
Add shortages to sales
rst-2-q104.explanation: Check partial amounts in opened goods. Box counts alone misstate actual quantities.

rst-2-q105.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q105.stem: Teaching a long serving sequence all at once confuses trainees. What training method applies?
options: Increase speed from the outset
Observe nothing until success
Change steps each time
Divide tasks and practice progressively
rst-2-q105.explanation: Train long sequences in sections, verify achievement, then connect to the next stage.

rst-2-q106.objective: Assess ingredients, cooking processes, and safe utensil handling.
rst-2-q106.stem: Food is served based only on an automatic appliance’s temperature setting. What improvement applies?
options: Remove checks because a display exists
Use without recording settings
Set every dish to the same maximum
Check actual temperature and finish too
rst-2-q106.explanation: Settings and actual temperatures may differ. Check equipment condition and proper food heating.

rst-2-q107.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q107.stem: A broken utensil returns to use and is found again. What system improvement applies?
options: Only use brighter plates
Define defective-item isolation and disposal/replacement procedures
Hide damage with cloth
Rely only on users’ memory
rst-2-q107.explanation: Break the reuse route by organizing identification, isolation, handling, and replacement.

rst-2-q108.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q108.stem: Complaint handover makes guests repeat explanations. What improvement applies?
options: Restart questions at every change
Pass only the prior worker’s impression
Remember without recording
Hand over facts and response history accurately
rst-2-q108.explanation: Share the complaint, confirmed facts, and promised actions to reduce repetition and conflicting responses.

rst-2-q109.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q109.stem: An allergy-adapted dish cannot be distinguished from ordinary food. What improvement applies?
options: Guess if plates match
Only kitchen staff need remember
Align identification and checks from order through service
Judge by the guest’s reaction afterward
rst-2-q109.explanation: Prevent mix-ups as well as checking ingredients. Identify dishes reliably through slips and handover.

rst-2-q110.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q110.stem: 5 people each work4 hours. What is total labor in person-hours?
options: 9 person-hours
20 person-hours
1.25 person-hours
80 person-hours
rst-2-q110.explanation: Person-hours are people×hours:5×4＝20 person-hours. Distinguish the4 elapsed hours of simultaneous work.

rst-2-q111.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q111.stem: A first-day trainee knows neither exits nor handwashing stations. What induction needs improvement?
options: Only popular menu prices
Only regular-customer gossip
Only memorizing sales goals
Facility layout and safety/hygiene rules
rst-2-q111.explanation: First-day induction teaches layout and work rules and explains responsible people and the training flow.

rst-2-q112.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q112.stem: Floors become dirty again after high ventilation equipment is cleaned. What process improvement applies?
options: Only clean floors twice first
Leave overhead dirt
Set a top-to-bottom sequence
Clean above exposed food
rst-2-q112.explanation: Plan for falling dust and protect food to reduce rework and contamination.

rst-2-q113.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q113.stem: If closing inventory is understated with all else equal, what happens to calculated actual cost?
options: Understated
Overstated
Always zero
Equal to sales
rst-2-q113.explanation: Actual cost equals opening stock＋purchases−closing stock. A smaller subtraction raises cost.

rst-2-q114.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q114.stem: A supplier changes specifications but the note and unit price match. Why still check?
options: It affects yield and finished quality
Specifications never affect cost
Same quantities always mean identical quality
Only photo colors change
rst-2-q114.explanation: Size and grade affect usage, waste, appearance, and taste. Unit price alone does not establish equivalence.

rst-2-q115.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q115.stem: Several guests report illness after the same dish. What takes priority?
options: Preserve facts/service history and contact necessary authorities
Discard records until cause is confirmed
Give different unshared explanations
Immediately deny restaurant responsibility
rst-2-q115.explanation: For suspected health harm, preserve records and items and coordinate appropriate reporting and investigation through the responsible person.

rst-2-q116.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q116.stem: Set menus shorten service time. What else should sales management check?
options: Declare permanent success from set counts
Effects on turnover, profit, and individual-item sales
Exclude discounts from costs
Discard à-la-carte data
rst-2-q116.explanation: Measure effects on efficiency and profit as well as sales to decide continuation or improvement.

rst-2-q117.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q117.stem: Sales are800,000 yen and cost of goods280,000 yen. What is gross profit?
rst-2-q117.explanation: Gross profit equals sales−cost of goods.800,000−280,000＝520,000 yen, distinct from operating profit.

rst-2-q118.objective: Understand restaurant operating figures and procedures and make improvement decisions.
rst-2-q118.stem: In drills the caller does not know contacts or messages. What improvement applies?
options: Make calling procedures specific and verify them
Add only role-name charts
Do not practice until the next disaster
Remove all evacuation roles
rst-2-q118.explanation: Prepare what to tell whom and how, then verify execution in drills rather than merely listing roles.

rst-2-q119.objective: Assess hygiene hazards and appropriate controls.
rst-2-q119.stem: Repacking refrigerated ingredients loses lot identification. What improvement applies?
options: Remember only the supplier
Give everything one delivery date
Reduce labels for neatness
Label so the original lot remains traceable
rst-2-q119.explanation: Preserve identification during repacking for recall and expiry tracing.

rst-2-q120.objective: Choose service responses suited to the customer’s situation.
rst-2-q120.stem: A worker’s tray tilts during bowing. What coaching applies?
options: Only deepen the bow
Practice safe movement and posture separately
Bend suddenly near guests
Demonstrate only after food falls
rst-2-q120.explanation: Service forms assume safe execution. Check carrying and greeting movements for the situation.

rst-2-q121.objective: Prevent pests according to their type and entry routes, and revise measures using inspection findings.
rst-2-q121.stem: An insect trap has stopped catching insects. What should be checked before concluding that pest control succeeded?
options: Judge only whether the previous pest-control work ended as scheduled
The installation location and whether the trap works effectively
If the catch is zero, consider visual checks for signs of infestation unnecessary
Assume that the longer the trap catches nothing, the more certain it is to be working normally
rst-2-q121.explanation: A zero catch may also result from a faulty trap or an unsuitable location.

rst-2-q122.objective: Check ingredient characteristics and labels to choose storage methods and customer explanations.
rst-2-q122.stem: Seasonal changes in vegetable size have caused uneven cooking. What should be adjusted?
options: Check the cutting method and cooking conditions against the vegetables' characteristics
Use the same cooking time without checking, regardless of the season
Skip checking the finished food
Serve the hard parts without explaining them to the customer
rst-2-q122.explanation: Reflect changes in ingredients in the process by comparing them with finished-product standards.

rst-2-q123.objective: Calculate costs from stocktakes and sales records and analyse causes with explicit signs for differences.
rst-2-q123.stem: Oversized portions occur frequently only during a particular time period. Which improvement is effective?
options: Observe and correct weighing practices and instruction during that period
Give all staff an unrelated lecture once
Abolish standard portion sizes
Only increase the size of the serving plates
rst-2-q123.explanation: Narrow down the conditions in which the problem occurs, identify its cause in the process, and adjust the work so that standard portions can be maintained.

rst-2-q124.objective: Compare purchasing routes and check additive purposes and conditions of use.
rst-2-q124.stem: Which additive function matches the intended use of making water and oil form a uniform mixture?
options: The function of a raising agent
The function of a bleaching agent
The function of a colour fixative
The function of an emulsifier
rst-2-q124.explanation: Different types of additives have different purposes; emulsifiers are used to make water and oil form a uniform mixture.

rst-2-q125.objective: Avoid assigning unwell staff to food preparation, arrange substitutes, and direct prevention of recontamination.
rst-2-q125.stem: Health reports have decreased because staff who report symptoms are teased by colleagues. What should the manager improve?
options: Tell all customers about the reporting employee's symptoms
Establish an accessible reporting channel and practices that do not disadvantage staff for reporting
Set a target to reduce the number of reports
Blame employees for reporting by treating it as an absence
rst-2-q125.explanation: A workplace environment that discourages reporting can lead to concealed symptoms and weaken preventive management.

rst-2-q126.objective: Organise competing requests around safety and quality and share customer information appropriately.
rst-2-q126.stem: An employee takes the reservation list home and saves it on a personal device. What is the appropriate response?
options: Allow unlimited personal storage if it is for work
Share the entire list on social media
Take no action until it is lost
Correct the practice in line with the restaurant's information-management rules
rst-2-q126.explanation: Manage personal information according to its purpose and access permissions, preventing private removal and disclosure.

rst-2-q127.objective: Select disinfection appropriate to the item and prevent recontamination from cleaning until the next use.
rst-2-q127.stem: An employee is about to put a heat-sensitive utensil in a hot-air storage cabinet. What is the appropriate decision?
options: Set the highest temperature to shorten the time
Check its heat resistance and a suitable disinfection method
If it deforms, push it back into shape and use it
Use the same method for every material
rst-2-q127.explanation: Choose a disinfection method to suit the utensil's material and shape as well as the microorganisms involved.

rst-2-q128.objective: Avoid assigning unwell staff to food preparation, arrange substitutes, and direct prevention of recontamination.
rst-2-q128.stem: An employee habitually touches the outside of their mask while plating food. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Exempt mask wearers from handwashing
Keep wiping the outside with a gloved hand
Check hand hygiene after touching it and how to wear it without touching the outside
Teach that touching the face makes the hands clean
rst-2-q128.explanation: Teach not only the wearing of protective equipment but also how to use it without causing contamination through contact.

rst-2-q129.objective: Compare purchasing routes and check additive purposes and conditions of use.
rst-2-q129.stem: There is a proposal to change suppliers. What should be compared besides unit price?
options: Decide only by the quoted unit price without checking minimum order quantities or lead times
If the unit price is low, do not check whether the required specifications and quantities can be supplied reliably
Quality, delivery terms, and stable supply
Switch entirely to the supplier offering the biggest short-term discount without comparing delivery terms
rst-2-q129.explanation: Compare the strengths and weaknesses of distribution channels and suppliers against the restaurant's requirements.

rst-2-q130.objective: Prevent pests according to their type and entry routes, and revise measures using inspection findings.
rst-2-q130.stem: Small flies repeatedly appear only around a drain. What should be the main measure?
options: Remove dirt from the drainage system and eliminate breeding sources
Only increase the frequency of killing adult flies and omit inspections inside the drain
Assume drain cleaning is unnecessary if chemicals are used outside opening hours
Only record catch numbers without investigating why the problem recurs in the same place
rst-2-q130.explanation: Use the pattern of where insects appear to investigate dirt in the drainage system and eliminate the breeding source.

rst-2-q131.objective: Prevent pests according to their type and entry routes, and revise measures using inspection findings.
rst-2-q131.stem: There are gnaw marks on a stored flour bag. What should the person in charge do?
options: Seal the hole with tape and use the flour
Assume sifting the flour always makes it safe
Turn the bag over and put it back
Isolate the affected stock and inspect the surroundings and entry routes
rst-2-q131.explanation: Stop using items suspected of contamination, and check other stock and the premises as well.

rst-2-q132.objective: Decide order quantities from forecasts and actual stock and match purchase orders, delivery notes and goods.
rst-2-q132.stem: When deciding an order quantity, confirmed deliveries for the next day are overlooked. What is the problem?
options: Quality standards automatically increase
Only stockouts will necessarily increase
Costs always become zero
Duplicate orders may cause excess stock
rst-2-q132.explanation: Check requirements, current stock, and scheduled deliveries together to prevent duplicate orders.

rst-2-q133.objective: Teach suggestions and telephone responses that suit customers’ wishes using clear words and expressions.
rst-2-q133.stem: Staff recommend dessert to every customer, including those who want to limit sweets. What should be improved?
options: Consider suitable options and the right timing for the customer's wishes
Keep recommending the same product even after refusal
Explain only the sales target to the customer
Cancel the customer's stated preference
rst-2-q133.explanation: Suggestive selling should improve customer satisfaction, rather than impose the same recommendation on everyone.

rst-2-q134.objective: Teach preparation with both taste and hygiene in mind and reduce variation in results.
rst-2-q134.stem: Service is delayed because dried ingredients were not rehydrated in advance. What planning improvement is appropriate?
options: Decide the start time based on the time required for rehydration
Wait until an order arrives to look up how to rehydrate them
Skip rehydration and compensate through plating
Keep all dried ingredients soaking in water at all times
rst-2-q134.explanation: Include preparation times and storage conditions in the work sequence.

rst-2-q135.objective: Secure health and safety first, record facts, actions and causes separately and prevent recurrence.
rst-2-q135.stem: Relief staff do not know where the AED is stored. What should be improved?
options: Tell only those who can use it where it is
Limit knowledge of the key's location to one person
Inform all relevant staff of its location, emergency contacts, and training
Rely solely on the explanation given when it was installed
rst-2-q135.explanation: Share equipment locations and emergency communication arrangements routinely so that they can be used quickly in an emergency.

rst-2-q136.objective: Prioritize contamination sources inside and outside the facility, and assign daily and periodic cleaning.
rst-2-q136.stem: Condensation on a wall drips onto food. What improvement to the cleaning plan is appropriate?
options: Protect the food and investigate the causes of condensation and ventilation problems
Only wipe the wall at the end of the month
Put a cloth over the food and continue operating
Only mark the spot where water drips
rst-2-q136.explanation: Manage the conditions causing condensation and contamination of food, as well as cleaning.

rst-2-q137.objective: Estimate labour-hours from indicators and allocate staff with skills, breaks and busy periods considered.
rst-2-q137.stem: There are surplus staff during quiet periods and too few during busy periods. What should be improved?
options: Only match the total daily headcount
Concentrate everyone at opening time
Reorganize staffing based on demand and tasks in each time period
Keep the same minimum staffing even during busy periods
rst-2-q137.explanation: Plan staffing to match demand and workload in each time period, not just the daily total.

rst-2-q138.objective: Prevent pests according to their type and entry routes, and revise measures using inspection findings.
rst-2-q138.stem: A pest-control contractor plans to place poisoned bait. What should the restaurant check beforehand?
options: How strong it tastes
How easily it mixes into dishes
Placement and management methods that prevent food contamination
A colour that is easy to see from the dining area
rst-2-q138.explanation: Pest-control chemicals require placement, identification, and inspections that prevent them from entering food.

rst-2-q139.objective: Judge acceptance and use by matching specifications with temperature history rather than declaring safety from appearance alone.
rst-2-q139.stem: Beef cuts of the same weight have different amounts of connective tissue and fat. What is needed for consistent recipe results?
options: Treat them as the same quality if their weight matches
Standardize cuts and specifications through purchasing standards
Hide the differences with expensive plates
Only make all the meat look equally thick
rst-2-q139.explanation: Differences in cuts and specifications affect taste, texture, and usable yield.

rst-2-q140.objective: Calculate indicators from sales, customers, gross profit and total working hours and explain their different meanings.
rst-2-q140.stem: Sales are unchanged, but ingredient costs have increased. If everything else stays the same, what happens to gross profit?
options: It increases
It stays the same
It decreases
It always exceeds sales
rst-2-q140.explanation: Gross profit is sales minus cost of goods sold, so it decreases by the amount of the cost increase.

rst-2-q141.objective: Check management suited to employment conditions and prepare new workers to begin safely.
rst-2-q141.stem: The person responsible for a new employee's first day will be absent. What should be prepared?
options: Give the employee a uniform and work location, and postpone explaining basic rules
A replacement and a handover of induction content and contacts
Leave no contact for the newcomer's questions or reports until the original person returns
Skip the equipment-layout and safety-hygiene orientation if the employee has experience
rst-2-q141.explanation: An onboarding arrangement must ensure continuity in explanations of safety, hygiene, assignments, and responsible staff.

rst-2-q142.objective: Teach suggestions and telephone responses that suit customers’ wishes using clear words and expressions.
rst-2-q142.stem: A telephone handler said the restaurant's name too quickly, and the reservation details were misunderstood. What training is appropriate?
options: Continue with only a louder voice
Do not say the restaurant's name
Practise speaking at an understandable pace and repeating details back
Skip confirming reservations
rst-2-q142.explanation: Facial expressions cannot be seen over the telephone, making clear speech and confirmation of information important.

rst-2-q143.objective: Prioritize contamination sources inside and outside the facility, and assign daily and periodic cleaning.
rst-2-q143.stem: Ceiling work is planned in a kitchen while it is operating. What coordination is necessary?
options: Start directly above the plating bench
Choose times and segregated areas that prevent dust from entering food
Rush the work without covering dishes
Judge only by a visual check after completion
rst-2-q143.explanation: Repairs also require coordination of work processes and operating areas to prevent food contamination.

rst-2-q144.objective: Specify purpose, method, tools, sequence, scope, quality and time and teach in four stages.
rst-2-q144.stem: A trainer keeps doing tasks that the new employee can already perform alone. What should be improved?
options: Do all tasks for the employee permanently
Delegate everything without checking
Assess learning progress and ensure the employee has opportunities to perform the tasks
Decide training completion solely by attendance hours
rst-2-q144.explanation: After a demonstration, the employee needs to carry out the task and be checked against the standard.

rst-2-q145.objective: Confirm customer wishes and coordinate seating, utensils and serving times as a team.
rst-2-q145.stem: A customer declined assistance, but an employee keeps trying to help physically. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Insist that the customer accept assistance
Respect the customer's wishes and respond when needed
Make the companion disregard the customer's wishes
Stop even greeting the customer because they declined
rst-2-q145.explanation: Confirm necessary accommodations with the customer rather than imposing assistance.

rst-2-q146.objective: Calculate indicators from sales, customers, gross profit and total working hours and explain their different meanings.
rst-2-q146.stem: Sales have increased, but gross profit is unchanged. Which factors should be checked?
options: Cost ratios and the sales mix
Conclude that profitability improved solely because customer numbers increased
Assume all additional sales become gross profit and do not examine costs
Examine only changes in total labour hours, excluding costs that directly affect gross profit
rst-2-q146.explanation: Check changes in the sales mix and costs, as well as sales, to identify why the increase has not produced more gross profit.

rst-2-q147.objective: Secure health and safety first, record facts, actions and causes separately and prevent recurrence.
rst-2-q147.stem: After a hair was found in a dish, a replacement was offered, but the customer declined. What is appropriate?
options: Serve the same dish again without permission
Remove only the hair and return the remaining food
Do not record the customer's wishes
Handle the bill and related matters according to the customer's wishes and the restaurant's authorization rules
rst-2-q147.explanation: Apologize, check safety, establish the facts, and respond according to the customer's wishes and the restaurant's procedures.

rst-2-q148.objective: Assign inspection, reporting and evacuation roles and protect customers and staff without dangerous independent actions.
rst-2-q148.stem: Grease is accumulating around a hood's fire damper. What management improvement is appropriate?
options: Wipe only visible areas and close the record
Stick paper over the grease
Check its operation only during a fire
Plan safe cleaning, inspections, and servicing
rst-2-q148.explanation: Grease accumulation contributes to the risk of fire spreading, so carry out prescribed inspections and servicing systematically.

rst-2-q149.objective: Confirm customer wishes and coordinate seating, utensils and serving times as a team.
rst-2-q149.stem: A child's chair protrudes into an aisle. What should be improved?
options: Push it into a place hidden from the kitchen
Consult the guardian and ensure both safe passage and safe seating
Fix it in the path used to carry hot food
Leave it until the restaurant is full
rst-2-q149.explanation: Coordinate not only seating convenience but also serving routes and the safety of the surrounding area.

rst-2-q150.objective: Organise multiple orders’ processes to meet safety, quality and service-time requirements together.
rst-2-q150.stem: An employee changed a simmering process to stir-frying without authorization. What should the person in charge check?
options: Skip checking the finished food if the total ingredient weight is unchanged
Match only the cooking time without evaluating the different cooking methods
Do not compare with standards if the employee tastes it and says it is fine
The effect on finished-product standards, including taste, texture, and safety
rst-2-q150.explanation: Changing the cooking method affects finished quality and process conditions, so it must not be done unilaterally.

rst-2-q151.objective: Use checks of heating, cooling and washing equipment to decide when to stop use or arrange maintenance.
rst-2-q151.stem: Too many plates are stacked in a dishwasher rack. What should be improved?
options: Pack in even more plates
Only increase the number of recorded operating cycles
Arrange an appropriate load so that wash water can reach the surfaces
Accept the load if only the exposed surfaces are washed
rst-2-q151.explanation: Even a functioning machine may clean inadequately if overloaded or if items overlap.

rst-2-q152.objective: Organise competing requests around safety and quality and share customer information appropriately.
rst-2-q152.stem: Serving hot food and clearing dishes from an empty table need doing at the same time. What is the basic coordination?
options: Leave the food and continue clearing only
Send everyone to clear the same table
Remake the finished food
Serve the food first and clear the table later
rst-2-q152.explanation: In normal situations, prioritize service to avoid deterioration in food quality. Safety emergencies take separate priority.

rst-2-q153.objective: Reconcile cash and cashless records and handle discrepancies and deposits securely.
rst-2-q153.stem: The cash in the register exceeds the recorded amount. What is the appropriate decision?
options: Treat the surplus as profit without investigating
Investigate possibilities such as giving customers too little change
Distribute it among employees
Deduct it from the next day's cash without authorization
rst-2-q153.explanation: A cash surplus may also mean a customer received insufficient change and suffered a loss, so its cause must be investigated.

rst-2-q154.objective: Compare purchasing routes and check additive purposes and conditions of use.
rst-2-q154.stem: Someone proposes that preservatives make hygiene management unnecessary. What is the appropriate decision?
options: Follow the additive's intended use and standards, and continue hygiene management
Allow unlimited shelf life if preservatives are present
Increase the amount used without authorization
Explain that they always kill every microorganism
rst-2-q154.explanation: Additives are used for specified purposes and under specified conditions; they do not replace normal hygiene management.

rst-2-q155.objective: Calculate indicators from sales, customers, gross profit and total working hours and explain their different meanings.
rst-2-q155.stem: Customer numbers are unchanged, but average spending per customer has fallen and sales have decreased. What should the analysis focus on?
options: A decrease in customer numbers alone
Changes in the mix of orders or discounts
Changes in inventory-count units alone
An increase in labour hours alone
rst-2-q155.explanation: Breaking sales down into customer numbers and average spending shows that this change concerns spending per customer.

rst-2-q156.objective: Use checks of heating, cooling and washing equipment to decide when to stop use or arrange maintenance.
rst-2-q156.stem: A gas range has an unstable flame that goes out during use. What should be checked?
options: Relight it without checking every time it goes out
Stop ventilation to protect the flame
Safely check dirt and the condition of components
Surround it with paper
rst-2-q156.explanation: Dirt from boilovers and similar sources can cause malfunction, requiring prescribed shutdown and inspection procedures.

rst-2-q157.objective: Teach care suited to use and material and prevent incidents and losses from breakage or measurement errors.
rst-2-q157.stem: An iron frying pan is being stored wet after washing. What care improvement is appropriate?
options: Leave it soaking until the next day
Keep it wrapped in a wet cloth
Mix the rust into food
Remove moisture and store it according to its material
rst-2-q157.explanation: Iron rusts easily if moisture remains, so use drying and care methods suited to the material.

rst-2-q158.objective: Assess initiatives through sales volume, profit and customer response and improve relationships.
rst-2-q158.stem: A low-priced item sells in large quantities. What should be noted in ABC analysis?
options: Its ranking by units sold may differ from its ranking by sales revenue
Both calculations always give the same ranking
Units sold must not be counted
Subtracting quantity from sales revenue gives the ranking
rst-2-q158.explanation: Quantity and sales revenue are different indicators and should be distinguished according to the purpose of the analysis.

rst-2-q159.objective: Set responsibilities and completion standards for preparation, closing and routine cleaning and hand service over safely.
rst-2-q159.stem: The dining-area staff's guidance on admitting customers after last orders conflicts with the kitchen's understanding. What should be improved?
options: Share admission conditions and the range of dishes that can still be served
Let dining-area staff alone promise every dish
Wait until customers order to decide
Rush closing tasks in the dining area
rst-2-q159.explanation: Coordinate customer admission and kitchen service near closing to avoid promises that cannot be fulfilled.

rst-2-q160.objective: Standardize sorting, storage, and removal of waste and prevent contamination by dirty water.
rst-2-q160.stem: A waste-removal trolley crosses a clean plating area. What should be improved?
options: Move the trolley faster
Pile waste higher just to reduce the number of trips
Remove the clean-area signs
Adjust routes or removal times to prevent contact
rst-2-q160.explanation: Plan waste routes so that contamination is not carried into clean areas.

rst-2-q161.objective: Calculate indicators from sales, customers, gross profit and total working hours and explain their different meanings.
rst-2-q161.stem: Subtract food cost of ¥90,000, labour cost of ¥80,000 and other operating expenses of ¥70,000 from sales of ¥300,000. What is operating profit?
rst-2-q161.explanation: Subtract all the listed operating expenses from sales. 300,000 − 90,000 − 80,000 − 70,000 = ¥60,000.

rst-2-q162.objective: Prevent pests according to their type and entry routes, and revise measures using inspection findings.
rst-2-q162.stem: A supplier leaves the receiving entrance open. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Spray insecticide onto food
Agree with the supplier on receiving, door-closing and pest-prevention procedures
Leave it open only when it is dark outside
Only count insects after they enter
rst-2-q162.explanation: Control entry routes during deliveries too, keeping the necessary opening time short.

rst-2-q163.objective: Teach care suited to use and material and prevent incidents and losses from breakage or measurement errors.
rst-2-q163.stem: Fragments of a metal scourer may remain in a container. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Mix small fragments into detergent
Use more metal scourers
Switch to tools suited to the container and check for fragments
Finish simply by turning the container upside down
rst-2-q163.explanation: Manage the material and condition of cleaning tools so that they do not themselves introduce foreign matter.

rst-2-q164.objective: Confirm customer wishes and coordinate seating, utensils and serving times as a team.
rst-2-q164.stem: Dishes for the same table arrive separately, leaving one person waiting a long time. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Keep all finished dishes at room temperature for a long time
Share each table’s progress with the kitchen and coordinate serving
Ignore waiting customers and attend only to faster tables
Change who ordered each dish without asking
rst-2-q164.explanation: Coordinate across departments to balance the progress of diners at the same table with food quality.

rst-2-q165.objective: Trace ingredient changes and possible cross-contact, and explain matters to customers without making unsupported claims.
rst-2-q165.stem: Old and new versions of the allergen list are both available. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Standardize the version and effective date and prevent accidental use of the old version
Let each employee choose a preferred version
Only replace the list’s cover
Discard one version without checking its contents
rst-2-q165.explanation: Version control must show which information is current, and changes must be checked.

rst-2-q166.objective: Compare purchasing routes and check additive purposes and conditions of use.
rst-2-q166.stem: Purchasing from a nearby shop is convenient, but the required quantities cannot be secured reliably. What decision is appropriate?
options: Rely on it for all supplies solely because it is convenient
Always use goods of unknown quality when supplies run out
Abolish purchasing standards
Compare supply conditions and consider multiple options
rst-2-q166.explanation: Choose supply routes that meet the restaurant’s quantity, quality and delivery requirements.

rst-2-q167.objective: Avoid assigning unwell staff to food preparation, arrange substitutes, and direct prevention of recontamination.
rst-2-q167.stem: An employee without symptoms says handwashing is unnecessary. What explanation is appropriate?
options: Healthy people’s hands are always sterile
Even people without symptoms may bring in contamination
Infection is always visible
Gloves prevent everything
rst-2-q167.explanation: Health checks and hand hygiene are separate measures; both are necessary.

rst-2-q168.objective: Teach suggestions and telephone responses that suit customers’ wishes using clear words and expressions.
rst-2-q168.stem: Staff repeat the same recommendation whenever a customer orders, although the customer has declined it. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Share the customer’s preference and limit suggestions to those needed
Recommend it more insistently whenever the customer refuses
Reduce service to customers who refuse
Force the customer to explain the refusal
rst-2-q168.explanation: Recommendations should improve satisfaction and respect the customer’s decision to decline.

rst-2-q169.objective: Assign inspection, reporting and evacuation roles and protect customers and staff without dangerous independent actions.
rst-2-q169.stem: Only the night-shift staff do not know what fire-safety checks cover. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Assume it is sufficient for daytime staff to know
Prepare only the night-shift records the next morning
Share roles and checking methods across all shifts
Close night-time evacuation routes
rst-2-q169.explanation: Fire-safety management needs a system and handovers that work during every shift.

rst-2-q170.objective: Organise multiple orders’ processes to meet safety, quality and service-time requirements together.
rst-2-q170.stem: Too many ingredients are prepared in advance and their quality deteriorates. What should the cooking plan include?
options: A policy of processing all stock every morning
A plan that omits checks of finished food
Preparation quantities suited to demand and safe storage duration
A policy of always carrying leftovers over to the next day
rst-2-q170.explanation: Plan preparation around the quantities needed and changes over time, as well as efficiency.

rst-2-q171.objective: Specify purpose, method, tools, sequence, scope, quality and time and teach in four stages.
rst-2-q171.stem: You want to explain hygiene principles to everyone and practise skills in the workplace. Which training arrangement is appropriate?
options: Teach all practical skills only through lectures
Omit all explanation of the principles
Issue attendance certificates without checking performance
Combine group knowledge training with on-the-job training
rst-2-q171.explanation: Combine opportunities to learn knowledge with workplace training for practical skills.

rst-2-q172.objective: Record attendance in line with actual work, and distinguish and check overtime, late-night work, holiday work and breaks.
rst-2-q172.stem: Attendance records end at closing time, but staff actually clean up afterward. What should the manager do?
options: Exclude all time after closing from records
Give additional instructions after staff clock out
Establish actual working time and correct records and work plans
Carry unrecorded hours over to the following month
rst-2-q172.explanation: Check discrepancies between actual work and records and manage working hours appropriately.

rst-2-q173.objective: Check measurement reliability and an environment that supports handwashing, and respond to faults without leaving them unresolved.
rst-2-q173.stem: Thermometer inspection results cannot be linked to equipment numbers. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Give every thermometer the same number
Keep only a list of readings
Try to remember the equipment by appearance when it fails
Identify each device and link it to its results
rst-2-q173.explanation: Identification and records must make it possible to trace which device’s reliability was checked.

rst-2-q174.objective: Secure health and safety first, record facts, actions and causes separately and prevent recurrence.
rst-2-q174.stem: The employee receiving a complaint blamed another employee. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Continue the staff argument in front of the customer
Stop responding if the responsible person is unknown
Ask the customer to find the person responsible
Accept the matter as a restaurant and establish the facts and response
rst-2-q174.explanation: Shifting blame does not resolve the issue. The restaurant must establish the situation and take necessary action.

rst-2-q175.objective: Decide order quantities from forecasts and actual stock and match purchase orders, delivery notes and goods.
rst-2-q175.stem: The interval between deliveries has become longer. What matters when revising the ordering plan?
options: Unconditionally order the same quantities as last time
Demand until the next delivery and quantities that can be stored
Change only the delivery date without checking stock
Buy unlimited quantities of every product
rst-2-q175.explanation: Reflect the changed lead time in required quantities, shelf life and storage capacity.

rst-2-q176.objective: Standardize sorting, storage, and removal of waste and prevent contamination by dirty water.
rst-2-q176.stem: Only the outside of a waste container is washed, leaving residue inside. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Hide the residue inside with a bag if the outside is clean
