Use deodorizer until the smell decreases and delay washing the inside until the next collection
Include washing and drying both inside and outside in the procedure
Assume that adding extra bags removes the need to inspect inside
rst-2-q176.explanation: Dirt left in the container can also become a source of contamination, so keep the inside clean too.

rst-2-q177.objective: Calculate costs from stocktakes and sales records and analyse causes with explicit signs for differences.
rst-2-q177.stem: There are 2,400 g of ingredients available for cooking, and the standard amount per plate is 120 g. How many standard plates can be made?
options: 12 plates
20 plates
200 plates
24 plates
rst-2-q177.explanation: Divide the available quantity by the standard quantity per plate. 2,400 ÷ 120 = 20 plates.

rst-2-q178.objective: Teach suggestions and telephone responses that suit customers’ wishes using clear words and expressions.
rst-2-q178.stem: Employees quote different prices when explaining a new menu item. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Align current product information and explanations
Adopt the higher price without authorization
Correct the price only at payment
Prioritize individual employees’ memories
rst-2-q178.explanation: Suggestive selling requires an accurate understanding of product details and prices.

rst-2-q179.objective: Use checks of heating, cooling and washing equipment to decide when to stop use or arrange maintenance.
rst-2-q179.stem: Equipment has been replaced, but only procedures for the old equipment are available. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Assume that the same dish requires the same operation
Update procedures using the new equipment’s manual and a trial run
Remove safety labels to make everything uniform
Do not inspect until a fault appears
rst-2-q179.explanation: Functions, operation and safety measures may change, so procedures and training must suit the equipment.

rst-2-q180.objective: Understand controls suited to the water source and equipment, and direct suspension of use and reporting when abnormalities occur.
rst-2-q180.stem: The area around a well has flooded, but the water is clear. What decision is appropriate?
options: Use it as before because it is clear
Use it with stronger seasoning
Taste a small amount before boiling to decide
Assess possible contamination and suspend use until checks are complete
rst-2-q180.explanation: After a disaster, do not judge safety by appearance alone; check the impact on the water source.

rst-2-q181.objective: Calculate costs from stocktakes and sales records and analyse causes with explicit signs for differences.
rst-2-q181.stem: Order-entry errors have increased the number of dishes that must be remade. Which measure improves costs?
options: Reduce portions below the standard
Extend ingredient expiry dates
Record mistaken orders as sales
Review order confirmation and communication to the kitchen
rst-2-q181.explanation: Order errors, as well as cooking errors, can increase the cost of discarded food.

rst-2-q182.objective: Trace affected products when problems arise after sale, and manage temperatures and labels during transport and display.
rst-2-q182.stem: Products subject to recall have been isolated, but changes in quantity are not recorded. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Remember only the isolation location
Treat all discarded quantities as zero
Record movements so that stock in, stock out and recalled quantities can be reconciled
Discard the original purchasing records
rst-2-q182.explanation: Tracing the location and quantity of affected goods helps prevent missed recalls and accidental use.

rst-2-q183.objective: Assess initiatives through sales volume, profit and customer response and improve relationships.
rst-2-q183.stem: Discounting increased sales volume but reduced gross profit. How should the initiative be assessed?
options: Continue unconditionally because volume increased
Compare the cost of discounting with additional profit and revise the initiative
Exclude costs from records
Record sales at the pre-discount price
rst-2-q183.explanation: Evaluate promotions by their impact on profit as well as sales volume.

rst-2-q184.objective: Compare purchasing routes and check additive purposes and conditions of use.
rst-2-q184.stem: You are checking the purpose of making cakes rise. Which type of additive serves this purpose?
options: Raising agent
Preservative
Colour-fixing agent
Emulsifier
rst-2-q184.explanation: Match the additive category to its purpose and check the stated conditions of use.

rst-2-q185.objective: Use checks of heating, cooling and washing equipment to decide when to stop use or arrange maintenance.
rst-2-q185.stem: An employee opens a steam appliance door suddenly and brings their face close to the steam. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Open it even faster
Demonstrate a safe opening and closing procedure that avoids steam
Rely on a hat alone for protection from steam
Have two people stand side by side in front of the door
rst-2-q185.explanation: Follow the equipment instructions when teaching where to stand and how to open and close it to avoid hot steam.

rst-2-q186.objective: Set responsibilities and completion standards for preparation, closing and routine cleaning and hand service over safely.
rst-2-q186.stem: After closing, only sales were checked, and leftover ingredients were not dealt with. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Allocate closing checks that include food handling and heat sources
Leave all work to the cashier without checking
Leave everything until morning staff notice
Push everything into a refrigerator out of sight
rst-2-q186.explanation: Closing duties include food and equipment safety checks as well as settling sales.

rst-2-q187.objective: Decide order quantities from forecasts and actual stock and match purchase orders, delivery notes and goods.
rst-2-q187.stem: Goods awaiting return are mixed into stocktaking. What is appropriate?
options: Separate them and clarify quantities and handling
Count them twice with ordinary stock
Hide the return supplier’s name
Count damaged goods as saleable
rst-2-q187.explanation: Organize returns and defective goods so that they are not confused with usable stock.

rst-2-q188.objective: Organise competing requests around safety and quality and share customer information appropriately.
rst-2-q188.stem: A printed sheet containing reservation information was left in the dining area. What response is appropriate?
options: Turn it face down and leave it in the dining area
Hide only some names
Allow anyone to read it during business hours
Collect it and review access, storage and disposal procedures
rst-2-q188.explanation: Paper lists also contain personal information and need controls against loss and disclosure.

rst-2-q189.objective: Reconcile cash and cashless records and handle discrepancies and deposits securely.
rst-2-q189.stem: A payment was cancelled, but the cancellation is not reflected in sales records. What response is appropriate?
options: Reconcile cancellation records on the terminal and register
Cover the difference in cash without recording it
Subtract an arbitrary amount from the next day’s sales
Charge the same customer again
rst-2-q189.explanation: Check consistency between payment and sales records to prevent double charging and identify discrepancies.

rst-2-q190.objective: Estimate labour-hours from indicators and allocate staff with skills, breaks and busy periods considered.
rst-2-q190.stem: During busy periods, work stalls because one employee cannot perform a particular task. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Plan skill development and staffing that allows colleagues to assist
Always concentrate every task on skilled staff
Stop explaining assigned duties
Lower the quality standard for the task
rst-2-q190.explanation: Plan training and staffing to share necessary skills and reduce dependence on particular individuals.

rst-2-q191.objective: Teach care suited to use and material and prevent incidents and losses from breakage or measurement errors.
rst-2-q191.stem: Dirt remains along grooves in a chopping board. Which cleaning improvement is appropriate?
options: Wipe only the flat surface
Soak it in water without checking
Work the brush into the grooves, considering the direction of scratches
Leave the dirt and only extend disinfection time
rst-2-q191.explanation: Remove dirt from grooves before disinfecting, and check the board’s condition.

rst-2-q192.objective: Make slip, cut, burn and entanglement hazards visible and improve working methods.
rst-2-q192.stem: New staff frequently suffer cuts, but only the manager keeps the accident reports. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Blame only those who submit many reports
Analyse causes and incorporate hazards and countermeasures into training
Discard every report of minor injuries
Set a goal of submitting no reports
rst-2-q192.explanation: Use accident information to improve procedures, equipment and training without discouraging reporting.

rst-2-q193.objective: Secure health and safety first, record facts, actions and causes separately and prevent recurrence.
rst-2-q193.stem: After an insect contaminated food, the insect trap’s lamp was found to have failed. What prevents recurrence?
options: Replace it and also correct the system that allowed the inspection to be missed
Stop investigating once the insect is removed
Replace only dining-room lights
Leave staff unaware of the equipment’s location
rst-2-q193.explanation: Establish inspections that maintain equipment effectiveness and procedures for responding to faults.

rst-2-q194.objective: Organise multiple orders’ processes to meet safety, quality and service-time requirements together.
rst-2-q194.stem: Unused heating equipment is kept hot for long periods. What should be revised in the cooking plan?
options: Increase the time spent heating empty equipment
Run all equipment at maximum heat simultaneously
Equipment operating times suited to the cooking sequence
Do not check why equipment is running
rst-2-q194.explanation: Plan cooking order and necessary heating to reduce wasted energy while maintaining safety and quality.

rst-2-q195.objective: Avoid assigning unwell staff to food preparation, arrange substitutes, and direct prevention of recontamination.
rst-2-q195.stem: You are unsure whether to assign an employee with a wound to plating. What decision is appropriate?
options: Assign them without checking if they say they are fine
Ask customers to judge by showing them the wound
Assign them on condition that gloves are never changed
Check the wound, protective measures and task before assigning work
rst-2-q195.explanation: Assess contamination from the wound and the nature of the task before deciding on protection or reassignment.

rst-2-q196.objective: Design work areas and sequences to prevent contamination of foods that will not be heated.
rst-2-q196.stem: Labels identifying fish for raw consumption and fish requiring cooking came off during work. What is appropriate?
options: Stop use until the fish can be identified and confirm the handling category
Decide that the fresher-looking fish is suitable for raw consumption
Mix them because their shapes are the same
Change a cooking-required label to a raw-consumption label without authorization
rst-2-q196.explanation: Do not judge suitability for raw consumption by appearance alone; preserve ingredient information and handling categories.

rst-2-q197.objective: Reconcile cash and cashless records and handle discrepancies and deposits securely.
rst-2-q197.stem: There is a proposal to have one person make night-time bank deposits. What decision is appropriate?
options: Transport larger amounts alone
Check the restaurant’s security procedures and a safe staffing arrangement
Tell passers-by the amount
Open and count the cash bag outside the restaurant
rst-2-q197.explanation: Transport and deposit sales proceeds according to the restaurant’s established safety procedures, including security precautions.

rst-2-q198.objective: Check measurement reliability and an environment that supports handwashing, and respond to faults without leaving them unresolved.
rst-2-q198.stem: There is no soap at the handwashing station, so staff wash with water alone. What should the manager do?
options: Treat the station as normal if water runs
Put out only a container of sanitizer
Replenish supplies and establish checks before they run out
Skip handwashing until the next purchasing day
rst-2-q198.explanation: Maintain handwashing facilities, including supplies, so that they can be used correctly whenever needed.

rst-2-q199.objective: Organise multiple orders’ processes to meet safety, quality and service-time requirements together.
rst-2-q199.stem: Meat of different thicknesses is grilled together, and only the thin pieces burn. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Only turn all pieces over at the same time
Assume the quality is equal after scraping off burnt areas
Add water to thin pieces and cook them for the same duration
Align ingredient specifications with appropriate heating conditions
rst-2-q199.explanation: Thickness affects heat penetration, so match ingredient specifications with process conditions.

rst-2-q200.objective: Check ingredient, equipment and shelf-life constraints, and explain options with dietary wishes and safety in mind.
rst-2-q200.stem: Staff cannot understand a foreign-language enquiry, leaving dietary restrictions unclear. What response is appropriate?
options: Decide which foods to avoid solely from nationality
Treat a nod as agreement to everything
Use a means or staff member that can confirm the details accurately
Omit explanations if the photographs look the same
rst-2-q200.explanation: Do not guess dietary restrictions; secure a way to confirm the details with the customer.

rst-2-q201.objective: Avoid assigning unwell staff to food preparation, arrange substitutes, and direct prevention of recontamination.
rst-2-q201.stem: On returning from cleaning to plating, employees only change their gloves. What must be checked?
options: Assume no hand treatment is needed if the new gloves have no holes
Hygienic handwashing before putting on gloves
Return without washing after removing cleaning gloves, even if no dirt is visible
Exclude handwashing when cleaning took only a short time
rst-2-q201.explanation: In addition to changing gloves, remove contamination from hands before returning to clean work.

rst-2-q202.objective: Use checks of heating, cooling and washing equipment to decide when to stop use or arrange maintenance.
rst-2-q202.stem: A steamer is not producing steam normally. What should the supervisor do?
options: Serve after the scheduled time without checking the result
Inspect according to the equipment procedure and check effects on the food
Bring their face close to the door to check
Remove safety devices and keep using it
rst-2-q202.explanation: Steam conditions affect heating. Safely check both equipment abnormalities and the food’s heating condition.

rst-2-q203.objective: Decide order quantities from forecasts and actual stock and match purchase orders, delivery notes and goods.
rst-2-q203.stem: A unit price was entered with the wrong number of digits when stocktake results were copied. What prevents recurrence?
options: Include checks of specifications, unit prices and entered values
Treat every discrepancy as waste
Only recount quantities
Remove the unit-price field
rst-2-q203.explanation: Stock value depends on both quantity and unit price; copying and calculations must also be checked.

rst-2-q204.objective: Calculate indicators from sales, customers, gross profit and total working hours and explain their different meanings.
rst-2-q204.stem: Gross profit stays the same while total working hours decrease. What happens to gross profit per labour-hour?
options: It decreases
It necessarily becomes zero
It becomes equal to sales revenue
It increases
rst-2-q204.explanation: Dividing the same gross profit by fewer labour-hours increases the indicator, but effects on quality must also be checked.

rst-2-q205.objective: Confirm customer wishes and coordinate seating, utensils and serving times as a team.
rst-2-q205.stem: Customers have ordered different dining formats, making the serving order unclear. What should guide the decision?
options: Always serve the most expensive plate first
Decide solely by customers’ nationality
The restaurant’s serving standards, the table’s progress and requests
Unconditionally stop everyone’s meal
rst-2-q205.explanation: Observe basic dining conventions while checking the restaurant’s standards and the customers’ circumstances, then adjust.

rst-2-q206.objective: Trace affected items when problems emerge after sale, and manage temperatures and labelling during transport and display.
rst-2-q206.stem: A recall notice stopped at one restaurant and was not passed to another using the same ingredients. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Extend notification to the affected lots and distribution destinations
Assume isolation at the first restaurant is sufficient
Assume the other restaurant’s stock is outside the recall
Keep using it until a written notice is prepared
rst-2-q206.explanation: Check where affected goods were sent and used, then recall them or suspend use across the necessary scope.

rst-2-q207.objective: Teach preparation with both taste and hygiene in mind and reduce variation in results.
rst-2-q207.stem: Water released after rubbing vegetables with salt diluted a dressed dish. What should be checked in the process?
options: Only increase the seasoning ratio without checking the earlier process that adds water
Only mix more often just before plating without standardizing drainage
Only extend the time after salting without specifying how to remove the released water
Standards for salt-rubbing and draining
rst-2-q207.explanation: Account for water released by salting, and standardize processing and quantities to suit the dish.

rst-2-q208.objective: Calculate costs from stocktakes and sales records and analyse causes with explicit signs for differences.
rst-2-q208.stem: Large quantities of fried food are prepared before orders and discarded unsold. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Avoid disposal by extending expiry without limit
Exclude waste from cost records
Manage production pace according to demand
Increase every customer’s portion
rst-2-q208.explanation: Reduce overproduction losses by managing demand forecasts, production quantities and storage standards.

rst-2-q209.objective: Assign inspection, reporting and evacuation roles and protect customers and staff without dangerous independent actions.
rst-2-q209.stem: An evacuation guidance light has failed, but nobody has reported it. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Close only during hours when it becomes dark
Establish inspection, fault-reporting and repair procedures
Have staff memorize the sign’s location instead of repairing it
Only test by switching off ordinary lights
rst-2-q209.explanation: Evacuation equipment needs a system that corrects faults as well as inspections.

rst-2-q210.objective: Select disinfection appropriate to the item and prevent recontamination from cleaning until the next use.
rst-2-q210.stem: Utensils are stacked tightly inside a UV storage cabinet. What matters when checking effectiveness?
options: Treat effects on overlapping surfaces as verified merely because power is on
Check only that the cabinet is full, without checking unexposed surfaces
Assume extending operating time slightly gives equal effects where light does not reach
Placement that allows light to reach the items and the lamp’s condition
rst-2-q210.explanation: UV cannot be expected to work on unexposed areas; check arrangement and effective irradiation.

rst-2-q211.objective: Assess initiatives through sales volume, profit and customer response and improve relationships.
rst-2-q211.stem: A seasonal menu was introduced, but regular-menu sales also fell. How should it be evaluated?
options: Only add up sales of the new items
Check effects on the whole restaurant’s sales mix and profit
Delete records of products with declining sales
Ignore all introduction costs
rst-2-q211.explanation: Evaluate the initiative including substitution away from existing products, rather than only new-item sales.

rst-2-q212.objective: Make fall, cut, burn and entanglement hazards visible and improve work methods.
rst-2-q212.stem: Employees enter a wet floor being cleaned without noticing. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Omit signs and traffic control if the cleaner knows the hazard
Only specify drying time and leave access decisions to individuals
Only put out a warning sign without checking visibility or a safe alternative route
Clearly identify and manage the cleaning area and walking routes
rst-2-q212.explanation: Communicate temporary cleaning hazards in a way others can recognize and control pedestrian access.

rst-2-q213.objective: Calculate indicators from sales, customers, gross profit and total working hours and explain their different meanings.
rst-2-q213.stem: With the same total working hours, sales increased while gross profit decreased. How do labour-hour indicators change?
options: Both necessarily increase
Both necessarily decrease
Sales per labour-hour increase and gross profit per labour-hour decreases
Neither changes
rst-2-q213.explanation: The direction differs depending on whether the numerator is sales or gross profit. Do not confuse the two indicators.

rst-2-q214.objective: Organise multiple orders’ processes to meet safety, quality and service-time requirements together.
rst-2-q214.stem: Frying oil keeps foaming and its colour and smell have changed. What decision is appropriate?
options: Compare its condition with standards to decide whether it can be used
Assume it is always usable after skimming the foam
Assume adding a little new oil removes the need for checks
Move it into a dark container to hide its colour
rst-2-q214.explanation: Check multiple signs of oil deterioration and decide using the established control method.

rst-2-q215.objective: Prioritize contamination sources inside and outside the facility, and assign daily and periodic cleaning.
rst-2-q215.stem: A fluorescent-light cover has a thick layer of dust. What precaution is needed when cleaning?
options: Brush it off directly above plating in progress
Catch dust with food-container lids
Prevent fallout onto food and safely stop affected operations before cleaning
Leave the cover removed
rst-2-q215.explanation: Overhead cleaning must consider both foreign-matter contamination of food and worker safety.

rst-2-q216.objective: Teach suggestions and telephone responses that suit customers’ wishes using clear words and expressions.
rst-2-q216.stem: An employee said “Certainly,” but nobody handled the request afterward. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Teach communication of the request through to confirmation of completion
Pass the employee if the wording alone is correct
Prohibit all replies
Have the customer find another employee each time
rst-2-q216.explanation: Service phrases must lead to action; repeat-back, handover and completion checks are necessary.

rst-2-q217.objective: Judge acceptance and use by matching specifications with temperature history rather than declaring safety from appearance alone.
rst-2-q217.stem: Acceptance standards for meat and fish say only “fresh.” What improvement is appropriate?
options: Use low price as the only criterion
Accept according to the receiver’s mood
Remove standards and return everything
Specify observable appearance, condition and product specifications
rst-2-q217.explanation: Set quality standards that different staff can check, rather than a single subjective word.

rst-2-q218.objective: Estimate labour-hours from indicators and allocate staff with skills, breaks and busy periods considered.
rst-2-q218.stem: You identify a tendency for customer numbers to fall on rainy days. What plan is appropriate?
options: Always use last year’s figures regardless of weather
Reflect weather and actual results in forecasts and check differences
Halve every product quantity each time
Determine quality solely from weather data
rst-2-q218.explanation: Include conditions affecting forecasts and check accuracy against actual results.

rst-2-q219.objective: Choose cleaning products according to dirt and material, and correct problems with labels, dilution, and storage.
rst-2-q219.stem: Dirt remains in a corner of a container labelled “washed.” How should acceptance be judged?
options: Ignore dirt if there is a label
Turn the dirty part to the back and use it
Check the actual container and restore it to standard by rewashing or other necessary action
Put it back until the next person notices
rst-2-q219.explanation: A label does not replace inspection. Judge usability from the actual cleaning condition.

rst-2-q220.objective: Specify purpose, method, tools, sequence, scope, quality and time and teach in four stages.
rst-2-q220.stem: A new employee follows the right procedure but greatly exceeds the standard time. What should be done first?
options: Observe the work and give specific support for the steps causing delays
Have them omit safety procedures
Repeatedly scold them only about time
Ignore the quality of the result
rst-2-q220.explanation: Observe method, quality and time together and provide the practice needed.

rst-2-q221.objective: Check management suited to employment conditions and prepare new workers to begin safely.
rst-2-q221.stem: The person explaining employment conditions and the assigned workplace give different instructions on uniforms and clocking in and out. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Let each first-day supervisor set rules freely
Unify current rules and communicate them during handover
Let new staff choose whichever instructions they prefer
Keep rules undocumented
rst-2-q221.explanation: Align basic onboarding information to reduce confusion from contradictory explanations.

rst-2-q222.objective: Connect general hygiene controls with control of critical process steps, and explain decisions after deviations and verification.
rst-2-q222.stem: The food hygiene supervisor proposes equipment improvements. What should the business operator do?
options: Check the reasons and hazards and consider necessary measures
File the paperwork without listening to the proposal
Assume qualifications remove the need to check the budget
Make the supervisor pay all repair costs personally
rst-2-q222.explanation: Make the role effective by using hygiene recommendations in actual improvement decisions.

rst-2-q223.objective: Secure health and safety first, record facts, actions and causes separately and prevent recurrence.
rst-2-q223.stem: A foreign object was kept after a report, but its connection to a particular table’s dish was lost. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Photograph it and mix the remaining items together
Record the item together with its serving information
Guess the table number
Confuse it with all dishes served that day
rst-2-q223.explanation: Cause investigation needs links to date, time, dish and serving destination, not only the physical item.

rst-2-q224.objective: Choose cleaning products according to dirt and material, and correct problems with labels, dilution, and storage.
rst-2-q224.stem: Someone proposes using an acidic detergent and a chlorine-based chemical together. What response is appropriate?
options: Assume more foam means greater effectiveness
Mix small amounts on one’s own judgment
Test the smell indoors to decide
Prevent mixing and check labels and safe procedures
rst-2-q224.explanation: Do not mix chemicals without authorization, to prevent hazards such as dangerous gas generation.

rst-2-q225.objective: Check ingredient, equipment and date conditions and explain in light of dietary wishes and safety.
rst-2-q225.stem: When checking an ingredient’s printed expiry date, you notice there is no opening record. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Use only the printed date indefinitely
Extend use based only on the container’s cleanliness
Have the next employee guess the date
Make opening date, time and storage conditions traceable
rst-2-q225.explanation: Opening changes the assumptions behind the printed expiry date; check the history and the restaurant’s use standards.

rst-2-q226.objective: Reconcile cash and cashless records and handle discrepancies and deposits securely.
rst-2-q226.stem: A shortage of change is expected, but no response was arranged before opening. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Leave everything to customers once change runs out
Give everyone excessive change
Prepare reserve change and a contact procedure for shortages
Erase the shortage from sales records
rst-2-q226.explanation: Forecast change requirements and establish an arrangement that also handles shortages accurately.

rst-2-q227.objective: Compare purchasing routes and check additive purposes and conditions of use.
rst-2-q227.stem: You are checking additives used to thicken food. Which category applies?
options: Colour-fixing agents
Bleaching agents
Sweeteners
Thickeners
rst-2-q227.explanation: Thickeners adjust viscosity and texture. Understand the uses appropriate to each additive category.

rst-2-q228.objective: Check ingredient characteristics and labels to choose storage methods and customer explanations.
rst-2-q228.stem: A local traditional vegetable was described as the same variety throughout the country. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Verify purchasing information such as region and variety
Continue the explanation if the shape is similar
Advertise while concealing its origin
Omit all vegetable names
rst-2-q228.explanation: Traditional vegetables are linked to local food cultures and varieties, so verify accurate information.

rst-2-q229.objective: Organise competing requests around safety and quality and share customer information appropriately.
rst-2-q229.stem: Customers are waiting both to pay and to order. What is the usual adjustment?
options: Have everyone take orders only
Leave both groups waiting without explanation
Prioritize payment and speak to waiting customers
Finish clearing every dish before taking payment
rst-2-q229.explanation: Use basic priorities together with explanations to waiting customers and assistance where needed.

rst-2-q230.objective: Calculate costs from stocktakes and sales records and analyse causes with explicit signs for differences.
rst-2-q230.stem: The standard cost ratio is 32% and the actual cost ratio is 35%. What is the difference in percentage points expressed as “standard minus actual”?
options: −3 percentage points
+3 percentage points
+67 percentage points
−0.03 percentage points
rst-2-q230.explanation: 32 − 35 = −3 percentage points. Keep the subtraction order and units consistent.

rst-2-q231.objective: Set responsibilities and completion standards for preparation, closing and routine cleaning and hand service over safely.
rst-2-q231.stem: The cleaner overlooks streaks on window glass. What training improvement is appropriate?
options: Only record cleaning time
Cover every window with curtains
Check the finish only on rainy days
Demonstrate tool use and how to inspect the finish
rst-2-q231.explanation: Teach concrete cleaning methods and checking standards, then assess learning through the actual result.

rst-2-q232.objective: Find specific shortcomings in quality, service, cleanliness and atmosphere and instruct staff on improvement.
rst-2-q232.stem: Service complaints have increased, but the manager only walks around just after opening. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Judge all hours solely by the morning impression
Also observe the times when problems actually occur
Do not record complaint times
Consider only regular customers’ opinions
rst-2-q232.explanation: Observe actual service under the conditions in which problems occur to identify specific behaviours needing improvement.

rst-2-q233.objective: Find specific shortcomings in quality, service, cleanliness and atmosphere and instruct staff on improvement.
rst-2-q233.stem: The entrance is clean, but tabletop condiment refill openings are dirty. What management improvement is appropriate?
options: Polish only the entrance more
Turn containers around to hide the dirt
Skip inspection if contents remain
Include customer-contact supplies in cleanliness standards
rst-2-q233.explanation: Keep checking cleanliness and hygiene beyond the entrance, including tabletop supplies.

rst-2-q234.objective: Connect general hygiene controls with control of critical process steps, and explain decisions after deviations and verification.
rst-2-q234.stem: The plan strengthens only heating to reduce bacteria, without changing how food is left afterward. What is its weakness?
options: It lacks control to prevent growth after heating
Assume reducing bacteria through heating removes the need to control subsequent storage time
Exclude cooling from records and control only the end of heating
Leave subsequent temperatures to each employee if no abnormality appears at completion
rst-2-q234.explanation: Hazard reduction and prevention of growth require separate controls, and the entire process must be considered.

rst-2-q235.objective: Organise competing requests around safety and quality and share customer information appropriately.
rst-2-q235.stem: Someone wants to use a customer’s telephone number for unrelated sales activities. What decision is appropriate?
options: Assume stored information can be used for any purpose
Have employees contact the customer privately
Check the purpose of use and restaurant rules, and stop inappropriate use
Give the customer list to an outside party
rst-2-q235.explanation: Manage customer information according to the purpose of collection and authorization, preventing improper or unrelated use.

rst-2-q236.objective: Standardize sorting, storage, and removal of waste and prevent contamination by dirty water.
rst-2-q236.stem: Unpleasant odours increased after responsibility for grease-trap cleaning changed. What should be investigated?
options: Only mask the smell with fragrance
Change the cleaner and erase records
Check what must be removed, actual cleaning practices and records
Blame only the collection contractor
rst-2-q236.explanation: Check whether the specified scope and frequency are being carried out and correct accumulated dirt.

rst-2-q237.objective: Teach care suited to use and material and prevent incidents and losses from breakage or measurement errors.
rst-2-q237.stem: A pan cannot heat because it does not match the heat source, despite having the same product name as another pan. What should be checked when purchasing?
options: Assume matching size and capacity make it usable regardless of material
The material and compatible heat sources
Buy it without checking heat-source compatibility if the pan name is the same
If it does not heat, turn the power to maximum without checking compatibility
rst-2-q237.explanation: Select utensils that match their intended use, material and heat-source requirements.

rst-2-q238.objective: Use checks of heating, cooling and washing equipment to decide when to stop use or arrange maintenance.
rst-2-q238.stem: Food cooks more slowly on one side of a griddle. What action is needed?
options: Investigate temperature unevenness and the heat source’s condition
Put all orders on the slower side
Explain uneven cooking as the customer’s preference
Assume it is normal based only on the displayed setting
rst-2-q238.explanation: Temperature distribution within equipment affects quality and needs actual measurements or inspection.

rst-2-q239.objective: Prevent pests according to their type and entry routes, and revise measures using inspection findings.
rst-2-q239.stem: A kitchen insect-trap light is clearly visible from outside. How should placement be revised?
options: Direct more light out of the window
Position it so it does not attract insects from outside
Illuminate only directly above food worktops
Choose its location solely by the number of insects caught
rst-2-q239.explanation: Even insect-control equipment must be placed to avoid attracting insects from outside or causing them to fall onto food.

rst-2-q240.objective: Use checks of heating, cooling and washing equipment to decide when to stop use or arrange maintenance.
rst-2-q240.stem: Oil and dust have accumulated behind a refrigerator, reducing cooling. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Only lower the setting and leave the cause unresolved
Pack in more food
Clean and service it according to the manual and check temperatures
Copy previous readings into temperature records
rst-2-q240.explanation: Check equipment conditions such as dirt around the cooling system and manage effects on food too.

rst-2-q241.objective: Select disinfection appropriate to the item and prevent recontamination from cleaning until the next use.
rst-2-q241.stem: A disinfectant’s expiry date is unknown, so effectiveness cannot be confirmed. What decision is appropriate?
options: Use it if its smell is strong
Check its condition and label and replace it with a suitable product
Add another chemical and use it
Only replace the container
rst-2-q241.explanation: Check chemical identification, condition and product instructions to achieve the required effect.

rst-2-q242.objective: Find specific shortcomings in quality, service, cleanliness and atmosphere and instruct staff on improvement.
rst-2-q242.stem: Plating looks good, but food reaches customers cold. What should be improved?
options: Only standardize photos of finished plating without measuring time after handover
Omit checks before arrival at the table if food is warm when cooking ends
Only increase servers’ trips without changing where or how long dishes wait
Serving temperature and the handover flow
rst-2-q242.explanation: Food quality includes suitable temperature and serving speed as well as appearance.

rst-2-q243.objective: Track ingredient changes and possible cross-contact, and explain uncertainties to customers without making unsupported claims.
rst-2-q243.stem: A purchasing label contradicts the restaurant’s allergen list. What decision is appropriate before serving?
options: Assume the restaurant’s list must be correct
Show both to the customer and leave all responsibility to them
Compare supporting information and avoid definitive claims until the discrepancy is resolved
Decide from the taste on the previous occasion
rst-2-q243.explanation: Do not leave discrepancies unresolved; check current specifications and align information accurately.

rst-2-q244.objective: Find specific shortcomings in quality, service, cleanliness and atmosphere and instruct staff on improvement.
rst-2-q244.stem: Employee appearance standards have deteriorated because checks rely only on self-reporting. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Do not check actual conditions if everyone has filled in the self-report
Judge cleanliness and correct wear only by whether a new uniform was bought
Leave standards entirely to individual interpretation despite repeated breaches
Provide specific standards and check them in the workplace
rst-2-q244.explanation: Share standards and check actual conditions to maintain a clean impression and hygiene.

rst-2-q245.objective: Check ingredient, equipment and date conditions and explain in light of dietary wishes and safety.
rst-2-q245.stem: Dietary restrictions other than allergies are treated as preferences that need no checking. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Make uniform assumptions about religion and beliefs
Assume removing meat always meets the need
Confirm what the customer avoids and what the restaurant can accommodate
Use ingredients without telling the customer
rst-2-q245.explanation: Respect dietary diversity and accurately connect the customer’s wishes with what the restaurant can actually provide.

rst-2-q246.objective: Manage subsequent temperature history and recontamination as well as heating conditions.
rst-2-q246.stem: A large order may exceed the equipment’s cooling capacity. What should be decided in advance?
options: Increase waiting time at room temperature
Leave the food at room temperature until next morning
Reduce only the quantity entered in records
Adjust quantities and processes to ensure safe cooling
rst-2-q246.explanation: Check cooling capacity against the order volume and adjust processes to meet control conditions.

rst-2-q247.objective: Decide order quantities from forecasts and actual stock and match purchase orders, delivery notes and goods.
rst-2-q247.stem: Stock entered in the automatic ordering system differs from actual goods. What improvement is needed?
options: Improve actual-stock checks and input accuracy
Do not check results because the process is automatic
Hide unsold goods from stock figures
Accept every excess delivery
rst-2-q247.explanation: Even automation cannot order appropriately if its underlying stock data are inaccurate.

rst-2-q248.objective: Confirm customer wishes and coordinate seating, utensils and serving times as a team.
rst-2-q248.stem: Another customer asks to change seats because of an assistance dog. What response is appropriate?
options: Always make the assistance-dog user leave
Feed the dog to draw it away from the seat
Protect the assistance-dog user’s access, hear both parties’ circumstances and adjust
Explain loudly without hearing either party’s wishes
rst-2-q248.explanation: Avoid assumptions about either party and adjust respectfully, considering access rights and those nearby.

rst-2-q249.objective: Teach preparation with both taste and hygiene in mind and reduce variation in results.
rst-2-q249.stem: A new employee damages fish flesh while removing scales. What training is needed?
options: Only make them work faster
Have them move without looking at the fish
Demonstrate direction and tool contact, then check their performance
Always cut off the damaged flesh and leave it at that
rst-2-q249.explanation: To standardize preparation quality, demonstrate specific tool techniques and check their execution.

rst-2-q250.objective: Compare purchasing routes and check additive purposes and conditions of use.
rst-2-q250.stem: Someone says additives of natural origin do not need usage checks. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Use natural additives without limit
Check purpose and conditions of use as well as origin
Declare them safe if their colour is pale
Replace specified quantities with visual estimates
rst-2-q250.explanation: Do not judge suitability only by origin; follow the necessary standards and labelling.

rst-2-q251.objective: Estimate labour-hours from indicators and allocate staff with skills, breaks and busy periods considered.
rst-2-q251.stem: Required labour-hours have been set, but only inexperienced employees work the same shift. What should be revised?
options: Assume there is no issue if total staff numbers match
Fix everyone on the same process
Completely omit guidance during busy periods
Check the combination of skills and supervision as well as headcount
rst-2-q251.explanation: Staffing plans must consider skills and roles, not only labour-hours.

rst-2-q252.objective: Organise competing requests around safety and quality and share customer information appropriately.
rst-2-q252.stem: While clearing dishes, an employee sees customers waiting at the entrance. What is the usual response?
options: Ignore them until every dish is cleared
Let them find empty seats freely
Speak to them and coordinate to prioritize seating
Block the path of a colleague carrying food
rst-2-q252.explanation: Follow basic priorities and coordinate within the team while explaining to waiting customers.

rst-2-q253.objective: Reconcile cash and cashless records and handle discrepancies and deposits securely.
rst-2-q253.stem: Someone proposes making an employee cover an entire cash discrepancy without evidence. What is needed first?
options: Investigate records and operations to establish the facts
Assume the employee is responsible
Delete discrepancy records
Charge customers again for the shortfall
rst-2-q253.explanation: Discrepancies can have several causes; begin with objective investigation and appropriate procedures.

rst-2-q254.objective: Connect general hygiene controls with control of critical process steps, and explain decisions after deviations and verification.
rst-2-q254.stem: The food-preparation location has moved, but hygiene-check locations are unchanged. What should be reviewed?
options: Contamination routes created by changes to movement paths and equipment
Keep only previous checking points if dish names are unchanged
Assume contamination risk is unchanged solely because equipment numbers match
Leave new routes to staff and do not check food and utensil crossings
rst-2-q254.explanation: Changes in process layout can alter hazards and checking methods, so reflect them in the plan.

rst-2-q255.objective: Use checks of heating, cooling and washing equipment to decide when to stop use or arrange maintenance.
rst-2-q255.stem: Cooked rice is abnormal, but there are many orders. What should the supervisor do?
options: Add seasoning and serve it all
Stop serving and check the cause and alternative arrangements
Skip checks because it is a popular item
Assume moving it to another container makes it normal
rst-2-q255.explanation: When equipment or finished food is abnormal, check whether service is acceptable; demand is no reason to serve noncompliant food.

rst-2-q256.objective: Set responsibilities and completion standards for preparation, closing and routine cleaning and hand service over safely.
rst-2-q256.stem: Reservation changes have not reached the kitchen before opening. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Unify change records and confirmation with relevant staff
Treat only the original booking sheet as correct
Leave verbal updates unrecorded each time
Adjust the headcount after serving
rst-2-q256.explanation: Establish a flow that delivers updated reservation information to both service and cooking staff.

rst-2-q257.objective: Find specific shortcomings in quality, service, cleanliness and atmosphere and instruct staff on improvement.
rst-2-q257.stem: Someone says staff do not need to greet each other because customers cannot see them. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Ignore each other when customers are absent
Use only fixed customer-service phrases
Treat greetings only as a numerical performance measure
Encourage greetings as actions that communicate willingness to cooperate
rst-2-q257.explanation: Greetings between employees help create a cooperative atmosphere and support service teamwork.

rst-2-q258.objective: Assess initiatives through sales volume, profit and customer response and improve relationships.
rst-2-q258.stem: A voucher intended to encourage a future visit is mistakenly applied to the bill on the day it is issued. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Give every customer an additional unconditional discount
Share the initiative’s purpose and eligibility conditions with cashiers
Determine effectiveness only by counting vouchers distributed
Hide mistaken applications as ordinary sales
rst-2-q258.explanation: Clarify the purpose and use conditions so that a return-visit initiative does not become merely a same-day discount.

rst-2-q259.objective: Record actual attendance and distinguish overtime, night work, statutory-holiday work and breaks.
rst-2-q259.stem: Training during work is omitted from working-time records. What should the supervisor do?
options: Delete all training time as outside working hours solely because it is called training
Ignore it unless the employee enters it
Check the actual training circumstances and treatment under labour management, then correct records
Leave it unrecorded because it generates no sales
rst-2-q259.explanation: Do not decide by the activity’s name alone; check actual instructions and participation and manage it appropriately.

rst-2-q260.objective: Use records for cause analysis and training improvement and check actual behaviour changes.
rst-2-q260.stem: Hygiene records are stored differently by each employee and cannot be found during an investigation. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Standardize searchable categories and storage rules
Only increase the number of records
Search using personal memory alone
Recreate missing records to fill gaps
rst-2-q260.explanation: Records need identification and storage that allow checking when needed; do not invent facts afterward.

rst-2-q261.objective: Prioritize contamination sources inside and outside the facility, and assign daily and periodic cleaning.
rst-2-q261.stem: A mop is placed directly on the floor after cleaning. What storage improvement is appropriate?
options: Hang it above food
Wrap it around clean dishes
Pack it wet into cardboard
Store it in a designated location where it can dry without transferring dirt
rst-2-q261.explanation: Store cleaning tools in places and ways that prevent recontamination and dripping onto food.

rst-2-q262.objective: Avoid assigning unwell staff to food preparation, arrange substitutes, and direct prevention of recontamination.
rst-2-q262.stem: The employee doing health checks assumes staff are well unless they volunteer a problem. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Specify check items and reporting methods
Always treat blank entries as normal
Do not ask about symptoms on busy days
Copy past declarations every day
rst-2-q262.explanation: Set daily health-check methods and operate them to prevent missed reports.

rst-2-q263.objective: Specify purpose, method, tools, sequence, scope, quality and time and teach in four stages.
rst-2-q263.stem: Trainers teach different procedures. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Let new employees choose their preferred method each time
Use different passing standards for each trainer
Adopt the fastest person’s method without checking
Confirm standards and align instruction
rst-2-q263.explanation: Reducing variation in teaching requires shared standards for purpose, procedures, quality and other requirements.

rst-2-q264.objective: Teach preparation with both taste and hygiene in mind and reduce variation in results.
rst-2-q264.stem: Fish is stored with moisture remaining after gutting. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Keep it fresh by soaking it for a long time
Return it to a container containing entrails
Check prompt washing and draining in the procedure
Absorb moisture with a dirty cloth
rst-2-q264.explanation: Control moisture and contamination after washing, and prepare and store ingredients appropriately.

rst-2-q265.objective: Choose cleaning products according to dirt and material, and correct problems with labels, dilution, and storage.
rst-2-q265.stem: Food enters gaps in a worktop that cannot be washed. What should the supervisor do?
options: Fill the gaps with a dirty cloth
Exclude them from regular checks
Dim the lights so they cannot be seen
Consider repairs or rearrangement that make cleaning possible
rst-2-q265.explanation: Do not leave difficult-to-clean structures unresolved; restore equipment to a condition where dirt can be removed.

rst-2-q266.objective: Decide order quantities from forecasts and actual stock and match purchase orders, delivery notes and goods.
rst-2-q266.stem: Delivered quantities match, but the product origin differs from the agreement. What receiving decision is appropriate?
options: Always accept it because the quantity matches
Check it as a discrepancy from agreed quality specifications
Change the origin label personally
Do not record it if it resembles the photograph
rst-2-q266.explanation: Receiving checks must compare agreed specifications such as origin and product standards as well as quantity.

rst-2-q267.objective: Judge acceptance and use by matching specifications with temperature history rather than declaring safety from appearance alone.
rst-2-q267.stem: Fish is inspected only by weight without checking eyes or gills. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Add freshness and quality checks suited to the fish
Accept heavier fish unconditionally
Do not inspect the goods if ice is present
Limit receiving checks to the delivery note
rst-2-q267.explanation: Check quality according to ingredient type rather than judging only by matching weight.

rst-2-q268.objective: Check ingredient characteristics and labels to choose storage methods and customer explanations.
rst-2-q268.stem: Leafy vegetables were boiled too long, harming colour and texture. What should be considered?
options: Hide it by increasing portions
Boil every vegetable for the same time
Heating and cooling procedures suited to the vegetable’s characteristics
Stop evaluating the finished food
rst-2-q268.explanation: Heating conditions affect leafy vegetables’ colour and texture; check ingredient-specific procedures.

rst-2-q269.objective: Compare purchasing routes and check additive purposes and conditions of use.
rst-2-q269.stem: Which explanation of a wholesale market’s role is appropriate?
options: It always makes all food ready-cooked
It handles functions such as gathering produce and price formation
It removes all need for producers’ hygiene controls
It guarantees identical retail prices forever
rst-2-q269.explanation: Wholesale markets contribute to stable supply through functions including collection, price formation and settlement.

rst-2-q270.objective: Organise multiple orders’ processes to meet safety, quality and service-time requirements together.
rst-2-q270.stem: The heating conditions in a procedure do not match the state shown in the finished-dish photograph. What response is appropriate?
options: Follow only the photo and ignore conditions
Decide according to each employee’s preference
Verify and align operating conditions and completion standards
Delete conditions from the procedure
rst-2-q270.explanation: A usable manual requires consistency between processes, finished quality and safety checks.

rst-2-q271.objective: Calculate costs from stocktakes and sales records and analyse causes with explicit signs for differences.
rst-2-q271.stem: A purchased weight of 8 kg yields 6 kg of usable material. What percentage is the yield, calculated as “usable weight ÷ purchased weight × 100”?
rst-2-q271.explanation: 6 ÷ 8 × 100 = 75%. Do not reverse purchased weight and usable weight.

rst-2-q272.objective: Secure health and safety first, record facts, actions and causes separately and prevent recurrence.
rst-2-q272.stem: Measures following a complaint were shared only with the employee concerned, and others repeat the same mistake. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Finish simply by transferring that employee
Keep every complaint detail confidential
Only increase the number of apology phrases
Share causes and necessary changes with relevant staff
rst-2-q272.explanation: Go beyond an individual response and incorporate learning needed to prevent recurrence throughout the work.

rst-2-q273.objective: Use checks of heating, cooling and washing equipment to decide when to stop use or arrange maintenance.
rst-2-q273.stem: Burnt residue sticks to a jet oven’s conveyor belt. What is the purpose of inspection?
options: Prevent foreign matter and effects on cooking results
Make the belt heavier
Automatically increase food quantities
Remove the need for cleaning records
rst-2-q273.explanation: Dirt on conveying parts affects foreign-matter control and cooking quality, so manage it using the prescribed method.

rst-2-q274.objective: Assign inspection, reporting and evacuation roles and protect customers and staff without dangerous independent actions.
rst-2-q274.stem: The emergency manual is locked away and the duty employee cannot use it. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Change storage and communication so it can be checked when needed
Treat storage of the original as completion
Have only one person memorize everything
Unlock it only during training
rst-2-q274.explanation: Provide access to information and understanding of roles so that emergency actions can actually be carried out.

rst-2-q275.objective: Standardize sorting, storage, and removal of waste and prevent contamination by dirty water.
rst-2-q275.stem: Water has backed up from a drain. What should the supervisor prioritize?
options: Continue normal cooking until the water recedes
Wash the floor with the backed-up water
Protect nearby food and work, and check the cause and extent of contamination
Assume no report is needed if it is moved to a waste container
rst-2-q275.explanation: Contaminated backflow can affect food and utensils; protect processes and correct the problem.

rst-2-q276.objective: Calculate indicators from sales, customers, gross profit and total working hours and explain their different meanings.
rst-2-q276.stem: Complaints and accidents are increasing during a period with high sales per labour-hour. What decision is appropriate?
options: Reduce staff further because the indicator is high
Evaluate workload and quality, service and cleanliness (QSC) alongside the indicator
Declare success if complaints are excluded
Omit safety checks to maintain the indicator
rst-2-q276.explanation: Productivity figures must be achieved without sacrificing quality or safety.

rst-2-q277.objective: Prevent pests according to their type and entry routes, and revise measures using inspection findings.
rst-2-q277.stem: Ingredient boxes are pressed against the wall, preventing insect checks. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Stack the boxes even higher
Store them with enough space for inspection and cleaning
Paint only the box exteriors every month
Stop inspections to avoid seeing insects
rst-2-q277.explanation: Storing goods away from floors and walls supports cleaning, pest detection and prevention of entry.

rst-2-q278.objective: Teach care suited to use and material and prevent incidents and losses from breakage or measurement errors.
rst-2-q278.stem: Someone tries to cut hard bones with a thin-bladed vegetable knife. What instruction is appropriate?
options: Assume any blade is suitable if enough force is used
Assume it is sufficient to look for broken blade pieces in the food
Have them hold the ingredient high by hand
Have them choose a knife and safe procedure suited to the purpose
rst-2-q278.explanation: Misuse can cause breakage and cuts. First check that the tool is appropriate.

rst-2-q279.objective: Set responsibilities and completion standards for preparation, closing and routine cleaning and hand service over safely.
rst-2-q279.stem: Another employee places dirty tools in an area that has just been cleaned. What improvement is appropriate?
options: Explain how to maintain cleaned areas and where tools belong
Only add more completion stamps
Stop checking the finish
Leave it until the next cleaning
rst-2-q279.explanation: Alongside cleaning itself, share practices to prevent recontamination with all staff.

rst-2-q280.objective: Calculate costs from stocktakes and sales records and analyse causes with explicit signs for differences.
rst-2-q280.stem: Waste of the same dish is concentrated on certain weekdays. What investigation is needed?
options: Compare only weekly totals without separating daily preparation and sales
Compare forecasts, preparation, sales and waste by weekday
Exclude high-waste days and assess costs only on normal days
Compare only employees’ speed without investigating demand forecasts and production quantities
rst-2-q280.explanation: Break comparisons down by the conditions in which waste occurs to identify causes such as over-preparation.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-1042e998f613.explanation: Fish with a large proportion of red muscle. Check the storage requirements for each species.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-3b5f57c01957.explanation: A parasite that may occur in seafood. Control it using the required freezing or heating conditions.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-72e1a5f519f0.explanation: A chemical used to reduce microorganisms at a concentration and by a method suited to the surface. It does not replace cleaning.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-ee999762d691.explanation: A virus that can also be transmitted through pork or wild animal meat and requires attention.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-923647be0f02.explanation: Basic hygiene controls for facilities, utensils, handlers and water, regardless of food type.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-60d9f126d7ab.explanation: Something that should not be in food. Its hazards vary with hardness and other properties.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-060387a831d3.explanation: A business serving food or drinks to customers. Hygiene and service must suit its operating format.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-f16f2d47d639.explanation: A pathogen that does not multiply in food like bacteria and may cause illness through people or other routes.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-d7d8d751cd44.explanation: Food poisoning caused through food or other items contaminated with viruses.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-4e4a87acf90a.explanation: A bacterium requiring particular attention when large batches of stewed food are cooled slowly.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-a3ef991efb45.explanation: A chemical using chlorine's action. Check its intended use, concentration, material compatibility and after-treatment on the product instructions.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-2a7b7c76af57.explanation: A bacterium that can transfer from skin or wounds to food. Heating alone is not sufficient to manage its toxin risk.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-b7c7ccd816c5.explanation: Expelling stomach contents. Stop handling food, report the symptom and take the necessary action.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-ba124451beca.explanation: The thickest finger. Do not miss its base when washing hands.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-3732e264dfa9.explanation: A measure of how hot or cold something is. Check the measuring location and unit.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-15752d3a15a6.explanation: Keeping food and storage areas within set temperature limits and taking action when conditions are abnormal.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-df6523d86621.explanation: An instrument for measuring temperature. Choose one suited to the surface, core or storage space being measured.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-9f84a83a0aa8.explanation: A defined band of temperatures. Control both the range and how long food remains in it.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-8a553c4ca859.explanation: A type of parasite that may enter the body through food or other routes.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-5789e02d74e2.explanation: Food poisoning caused by harmful chemicals entering food or similar contamination.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-1a6ef44c59bd.explanation: A product made by cutting, heating, seasoning or otherwise treating raw materials. Check its label and specification.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-161b501b8eec.explanation: Applying heat to food or other items. Safety checks also consider core temperature and time.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-76e751e1a7a9.explanation: A required part has not reached the necessary temperature for the necessary time.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-9200e9a9063c.explanation: A highly resistant form produced by some bacteria. It can survive ordinary heating.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-4cf29d199cb3.explanation: Food coated in flour or similar ingredients and deep-fried. Check core heating appropriate to quantity and thickness.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-979d721bde05.explanation: A type of dish using spices. Manage cooling, storage and reheating after large-batch cooking.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-d0d163dd0cf6.explanation: Removing or reducing moisture. It is also important for hygiene after washing utensils.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-96dd1a2b5b5c.explanation: A bacterium associated with risks from undercooked poultry and cross-contamination.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-1376f8d79f08.explanation: A condition set in advance to judge whether a process or state is acceptable.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-c6ce93114a36.explanation: Examining causes of illness at each process step and considering how to control them.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-5b542f51ce5e.explanation: The temperature band described in the material as favorable for microbial growth in food. Also control time spent in it.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-4af596e0fbf8.explanation: An organism living on or in another organism. Select appropriate controls for each food.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-5fca274f9cf9.explanation: Food poisoning caused by parasites present in food or similar exposure.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-12fb9d9cff10.explanation: A business providing goods or services. Confirm delivery contacts and trading conditions.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-bf94dc72b905.explanation: Information preserving actual checks and actions so they can be traced later.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-534263b04f24.explanation: Equipment separating and collecting fat from wastewater. Clean it regularly.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-44e9d89ed553.explanation: Stools looser than usual. Report it before handling food.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-753bfd13c7e7.explanation: Microorganisms, natural toxins, chemicals or other substances causing food poisoning or similar harm.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-fb95e9c5888e.explanation: Checking health and linking abnormal findings to reporting and appropriate work decisions.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-c11e6e63b1af.explanation: Adverse effects on health, including illness and injury.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-636ece1c7940.explanation: Contamination transferred to another food through food, hands, utensils or other routes.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-9710abf62596.explanation: Hard objects such as metal, glass or stones that may injure teeth or the mouth.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-3c9f92d7ecf6.explanation: Workplace management combining sorting, orderly storage, cleaning, cleanliness and sustained habits.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-569cd1b8b499.explanation: Rice cooked with water. Control its temperature and time until service.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-b0482fc20a17.explanation: Microorganisms that multiply in food or elsewhere under suitable conditions. Some cause food poisoning.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-ea4df4a25cf4.explanation: Food poisoning involving bacteria themselves or the toxins they produce.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-ff27b2861e7b.explanation: The ordered flow of receiving, preparation, heating, cooling, service and other steps.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-4c2cde896458.explanation: A surface for preparation or plating. Keep it clean according to the work category.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-36930458f2b0.explanation: A dish of sliced raw seafood. Confirm raw-material suitability and hygiene requirements.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-7a0a5bf124c2.explanation: A treatment that kills microorganisms; it does not necessarily mean complete removal of every microorganism.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-c2004add1c89.explanation: A collective term for various microorganisms other than the target. Assess specific hazards separately.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-4378fdddc5d4.explanation: A chemical used to control insects. Prevent contamination of food and harmful effects after use.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-f2abccadf217.explanation: A group of bacteria requiring attention when handling eggs, meat and similar foods.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-4d34a1938119.explanation: The temperature of a room. It varies and does not itself mean safe food storage.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-82213712d6ae.explanation: The amount of moisture in the air, measured separately from temperature.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-50c5bb3de736.explanation: Using education and checks to maintain the agreed hygiene behaviors.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-183c5056f86d.explanation: A step requiring particular control to prevent, eliminate or reduce a hazard to an acceptable level.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-b5fa071de23b.explanation: A part of food preparation requiring particular checking and control. Define the target and checking method.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-37054ad9f3b6.explanation: Rings, watches, necklaces and similar items. Prevent contamination and items falling into food during handling.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-c11af6e7553d.explanation: Treatment reducing disease-causing microorganisms to prevent infection and similar harm.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-0d85098a678c.explanation: The date indicating safe consumption of an unopened product stored as labeled.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-df11dd94b784.explanation: The date indicating how long an unopened product stored as labeled is expected to retain good eating quality.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-098294eeccc2.explanation: Equipment illuminating the work area. Check brightness, damage and dirt.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-acc1bb15d37c.explanation: Illness caused through food or drink. Causes include more than bacteria.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-31e51ceb3a80.explanation: Prevent bacteria from entering food, prevent their multiplication and destroy them.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-94df6ee7a6e3.explanation: Food fragments and dirt left after work or meals that can support insects and microorganisms.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-12b3f8ae1397.explanation: A basin for washing food or utensils. Keep uses separate and clean it after work.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-1e1a0f377b56.explanation: A control used to release flushing water. Clean it as a hand-contact contamination surface.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-ac60b7633187.explanation: Water supplied through a public water system. Also check storage tanks and other controls before it reaches the store.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-c3efd63354cb.explanation: A group of liquid dishes using vegetables, meat or other ingredients. Check materials, process and storage for each dish.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-6a09a2cc240e.explanation: A dish made by grilling or frying a cut of meat or similar food. Heating must suit the material and processing state.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-468ae5d8d33f.explanation: Maintaining hygienic conditions through sorting, orderly storage, cleaning and related measures.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-888dda3afd8c.explanation: Removing dirt and waste. Define targets, steps, frequency and checking methods.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-556384dc400c.explanation: Processing raw materials to make products; some steps may overlap with cooking.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-d96aee03758f.explanation: Setting locations and quantities for necessary items so they can be retrieved easily.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-ff0934736802.explanation: Separating needed from unneeded items and reducing what is not needed.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-03546d695ff0.explanation: An instrument using infrared radiation from a surface to measure its temperature. It cannot directly measure core temperature.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-96f0e7ea570a.explanation: A spore-forming bacterium requiring attention when handling cereals and similar foods.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-7146a1c1755d.explanation: A product used to remove dirt. Check the intended use and concentration.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-ec87f9dc89b3.explanation: A product for removing dirt from utensils or food. Check the permitted targets for each product.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-25af08d3d5c8.explanation: The condition indicating how fresh food is. Assess separately whether it is suitable for raw consumption.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-003741059728.explanation: A liquid or similar seasoning adding flavor or appearance. Check ingredients and storage conditions.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-990d02f679ba.explanation: A change from normal health. Do not diagnose a customer's symptoms; arrange necessary help.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-bca44fda3241.explanation: A passage carrying exhaust or other air. Watch for accumulated grease and dust.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-18d182ac3d10.explanation: A seasoned liquid for dipping, soaking or pouring. Control contact with raw food and separate uses.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-8d0b6fc41888.explanation: The temperature at the center of food. Check the measuring position when verifying heating or cooling.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-f7a67c0ebde4.explanation: A bacterium associated with seafood. Apply cold storage controls and prevent cross-contamination.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-a2ba28d427f5.explanation: A bacterium that may spread through meat and cause severe illness even in small quantities.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-925a2ab170f6.explanation: A place for washing hands. Keep necessary supplies available and do not store food there.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-e0531ea54e44.explanation: Cleaning on a defined cycle, separate from daily cleaning.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-27fc9f97c742.explanation: The inner surface of the hand. Wash it together with fingertips and spaces between fingers.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-cdb9b6e0d788.explanation: Protective items separating hands from food or dirt. They do not replace handwashing and require appropriate changing.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-7fe94c2c8bb0.explanation: The part gripped to open or close a door. Clean it because many people touch it.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-8544ed1121e9.explanation: A place for excretion. Keep its cleaning tools and footwear separate from the kitchen.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-fe3e7d57cb9e.explanation: Moist waste from food. Store properly, for example in lidded containers.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-5f5cb4404e36.explanation: Salad mainly using raw vegetables. Prevent contamination after washing and maintain low temperatures.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-9d322ab4bda9.explanation: Relatively soft objects such as hair, paper or flexible film.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-c8c3c832ef4f.explanation: Contamination transferred again to a cleaned item or food after processing.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-2e3640ca9202.explanation: Cleaning carried out alongside daily business and work.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-1fa4bfdaa118.explanation: A record of the day's checks, work, abnormalities and actions.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-4d68f6a1904b.explanation: Shellfish with two shells. Check intended use and controls against viruses and other hazards.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-bd4494a25cf9.explanation: Goods or raw materials reaching the store. Check the actual items when receiving them.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-44ba5684ac05.explanation: Water at a high temperature. Prevent scalds and check treatment temperature and time.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-db48b6cdc9ff.explanation: A supplier bringing ordered goods. Match the order against the actual items.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-615175b9214d.explanation: A chemical used against crop pests or diseases. Prevent improper contamination of food.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-00271a2debc0.explanation: A virus spread through infected people, food or other routes. Health reporting and handwashing are also important.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-db53e8f9ee96.explanation: Properly separating and disposing of items no longer intended for use or sale.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-f03df65eabde.explanation: Items no longer needed in business and intended for disposal. Follow classification and collection requirements.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-fc925f16649a.explanation: A channel carrying used water. Prevent buildup of waste and dirt.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-3388f672a17a.explanation: Cooking oil no longer used. Collect it as specified and do not pour it into drains.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-049626c75b3f.explanation: A hygiene approach analyzing hazards at each step and linking them to key controls, records and verification.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-d864fab7831d.explanation: A cause or condition leading to an accident or abnormality. Examine people, materials, processes and environment.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-2b2c6da3fb58.explanation: Material covering a wound. Apply necessary protection and checks to prevent it falling into food.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-eb59dcb84dc3.explanation: A dish of shaped ground meat or similar ingredients. Verify adequate heating to the center.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-4ebf3eb82852.explanation: A substance that may accumulate in some fish when stored improperly. Later heating cannot restore safety.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-cde0f0b12755.explanation: A dish serving tofu cold. Keep the final unheated preparation step hygienic.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-49ca56ced815.explanation: A term for insects and other contaminants causing strong disgust to the person eating.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-737dfcc35119.explanation: Bacteria arranged like grape clusters. Food poisoning controls particularly consider S. aureus and related bacteria.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-36328c788263.explanation: Chicken fried in oil. Check core heating, not just the exterior color.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-519c9e4a3203.explanation: A fixture receiving excreta. Clean and disinfect it together with surrounding contact surfaces.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-504af63e2af8.explanation: The part sat on. Clean it as a surface touched by hands and the body.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-53f8af709887.explanation: A blade for cutting food. Check designated use, blade condition and storage location.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-8247b558163c.explanation: The raised area at the base of the thumb on the palm. Do not miss it when washing hands.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-a3030bf8f16d.explanation: Keeping food under appropriate conditions to manage quality and safety until use.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-593f1629c120.explanation: Temperature, container, period and other conditions specified on the label or in the plan.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-2ff3914e3306.explanation: A salad using cooked potatoes or similar ingredients. Control cooling and contamination during subsequent mixing.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-e3ae12129e05.explanation: A board for cutting food. Separate uses and check damage and unwashed residues.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-cab13ca37b5a.explanation: Fish cooked by grilling. Serve with clean utensils and prevent recontamination after heating.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-fef547208e0a.explanation: Chicken or other ingredients grilled on skewers. Consider heating differences caused by cuts and thickness.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-2af9001a0cc8.explanation: A chemical product used for cleaning, disinfection or pest control. Clearly distinguish names and uses.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-0c806d3c7818.explanation: One of the five digits of the hand. Also wash between fingers and around nails.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-8ea42fe9b23e.explanation: The end of a finger, often touching food. Check it during handwashing.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-0fb688b74cfb.explanation: Water in motion, distinct from standing water, used for rinsing and similar tasks.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-6cac16b39789.explanation: Lowering food temperature. Control the core temperature and elapsed time.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-8069ff3152b0.explanation: Equipment cooling food or other items. Distinguish refrigerated storage from rapid chilling.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-f24011c239f1.explanation: Equipment storing food cold. Check actual internal temperature and storage period.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-0ea176c4f622.explanation: Equipment storing food frozen or in similar conditions. It does not kill all microorganisms.

rst-gloss-1-hygiene-273b56a9e3de.explanation: A term for cooking equipment. Confirm whether it means a gas range, microwave or another appliance.

rst-gloss-1-cooking-b15792cd291d.explanation: An appliance heating compatible pans through electromagnetic induction. Check suitable materials.

rst-gloss-1-cooking-d762da4573e3.explanation: Finishing a dish by mixing ingredients with seasonings or dressing.

rst-gloss-1-cooking-087d6efff6b5.explanation: A pan holding oil for deep-frying. Follow oil-volume and safety requirements.

rst-gloss-1-cooking-acbd0a5ac2b2.explanation: Cooking food immersed in hot oil.

rst-gloss-1-cooking-082b73325e76.explanation: A bivalve used in soup or steamed dishes. Check shell damage and freshness.
